sdd.audience: the five personas named in [PVD §4](PVD.md): **developer-authors** (the primary audience for the structured editing, AI assistance, and merge surfaces); **tech leads / reviewers** (the audience for the diff- and PR-review-friendly generated documents); **QA / verification engineers** (the audience for the STP and the per-test traceability annotations); **auditors / external stakeholders** (the audience for the self-contained Markdown traceability matrix); and **tooling integrators** (the audience for the JSON-RPC sidecar). overview.para: `TR` (TraceR) is a repository-native traceability toolkit. A single XML file (`doc/Project.xml`) holds the design, the high-level requirements, the low-level requirements, the test catalogue, and every cross-reference between them. A renderer turns that file into five Markdown documents (SDD, HLRs, LLRs, STP, Traceability Matrix); a linter validates it; a JSON-RPC sidecar exposes the same operations to a VS Code extension and a planned web form; an AI authoring layer drafts and reviews content under a strict validate-then-retry contract; and a structural three-way merger keeps Git merges of `Project.xml` sane.

The unifying design choice (`PVD §5`) is that **the spec documents are an output, not an input**. Every authoring surface edits the structured source and lets the renderer produce the prose. This SDD documents the components that enforce that contract; the SDP ([doc/SDP.md](SDP.md)) documents the *plan* to build them.

The architecture is deliberately **schema-driven from Phase 2.5 onwards** ([PVD §6 Principle 11](PVD.md)). The VS Code extension's tree, code lenses, form panels, document-render commands, and Markdown preview are built at runtime from `tools/project.xsd` UI hints (`xs:appinfo`) and the `<metadata><document>` list, so adding a new generated document or payload section is a schema-and-template change with zero TypeScript involvement. Bespoke widgets and domain-specific lint rules remain the only payload-aware code paths.

Several capabilities are deliberately **deferred to the PVD roadmap themes** ([PVD §9](PVD.md)) and therefore have no module in this SDD: the standalone web form (covered by its own plan); editor breadth beyond VS Code (JetBrains, Neovim, generic LSP); output-format breadth (HTML, PDF, DITA); schema-evolution migration tooling; and the optional `<plan>`-payload phasing overlay. Each is gated on demand and on Phase 1–5.5 having stabilised; when one is adopted, this SDD gains a corresponding module under [SDD §2.1 System Architecture](#21-system-architecture).

definitions.term: The single source of truth. Holds `<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, plus `<metadata>` describing each generated document. Lives at `doc/Project.xml`. Authored through structured surfaces; never edited as raw XML on the critical path.
A top-level child of `<project>` (`<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, or any future schema-declared section like `<plan>`) whose data is rendered into one or more Markdown documents.
A `.md` file under `doc/` produced by the renderer from `Project.xml` plus a Jinja2 template. Listed in `<metadata><document id="…"/>`. Never edited by hand.

`tools/project_io.py` — the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 server that every UI surface calls into. Owns parsing, validation, rendering, AI requests, and the structural merger. Spawned per extension activation; killed on deactivate.

An `xs:appinfo` annotation in `tools/project.xsd` (under the `https://tracer.dev/ui/1` namespace) that tells the extension how to surface a schema element: `ui:treeNode`, `ui:form`, `ui:lens`, `ui:document`. The hint registry is the contract between schema authors and the schema-driven extension surfaces.
The runtime dictionary built by `project_io.parse_to_json` from the XSD's UI hints. Drives the tree view, lens provider, locator, and form-field generator without per-payload TypeScript code.
A `<trace target="…" ref="…"/>` element on an HLR, LLR, or test, naming the upstream item it implements or verifies. The basis for the computed forward and reverse traceability matrix.
An HLR or LLR not referenced by any downstream `<trace>`. Listed explicitly in `Traceability.md`; surfaced as a lint warning and a tree-view badge. Never silently hidden.

The deterministic packed payload (`tools/ai/context.py`) sent to the language model on every AI request: schema subtree, `Schema_Reference.md` excerpt, PVD excerpt, relevant SDD/HLR/LLR context, sibling items, and the lint state of the target. Bounded by `projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens`.

A named AI operation (`draft.hlr`, `draft.pvd`, `expand.hlr_to_llrs`, `review.item`, `merge.body`, …) with its own prompt template (`tools/ai/intents/`) and JSON response schema (`tools/ai/schemas/`). Responses are typed JSON, never raw XML.

The AI pipeline (`tools/ai/pipeline.py`) that parses an AI response against its intent schema, applies it as a JSON Patch on a copy of the tree, runs XSD + lint, and on failure retries with the validator output fed back. After max retries the suggestion is surfaced to the user instead of written.

The deterministic structural three-way merge (`tools/project_merge.py`) over the parsed `Project.xml` tree. Re-keys elements by id, unions non-overlapping additions, unions `<traces>`, recomputes `<counts>`. No AI, no network.

The AI-mediated resolution of residual conflicts left by Stage A: overlapping body edits, divergent trace targets, ID renames, schema-version bumps. Runs through the same validate→retry pipeline as authoring intents.
The `schema_version` attribute on `<project>`. Bumped whenever `Project.xml`'s structure changes in a way existing templates or `render_doc.py` could not consume unchanged.

architecture.intro: The system is a Python core surrounded by editor-native shells. The Python core (`render_doc.py`, `lint_project.py`, `project_merge.py`, `tools/ai/`) is invoked by the long-running JSON-RPC sidecar (`project_io.py`). All UI surfaces — the VS Code extension, the planned web form, AI assistants — speak only to the sidecar; none of them re-implement parsing, rendering, linting, or merging.
architecture.component: the structured source of truth that every other component reads or writes; XSD-validated and lint-validated.
the schema, including (from Phase 2.5) the `xs:appinfo` UI-hint vocabulary that drives the schema-driven extension surfaces. The hint registry is built from this file at sidecar startup.
per-document Jinja2 templates. One per `<metadata><document>` entry. Templates own all spec-doc scaffolding (headings, numbering, tables); payloads carry only content.

the renderer. CLI for batch regeneration plus an importable library API (`render_to_str`, `parse_project_to_dict`) called by the sidecar. Never spawns a sub-process; never writes files outside its `--out` argument.
the linter. CLI plus an importable `lint(tree)` library API. Validates well-formedness, XSD conformance, ID format and uniqueness, broken trace references, and coverage gaps.
the deterministic three-way structural merger (Stage A of the merge pipeline). Operates on the parsed-dict representation from `render_doc.parse_project_to_dict`.
the Python AI pipeline: `context.py` (grounding bundle assembler), `pipeline.py` (validate→retry loop), `intents/` (per-intent prompt templates), `schemas/` (per-intent JSON response schemas).

the JSON-RPC 2.0 sidecar over stdin/stdout. Methods: `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `apply_edit(json_patch)`, `init_project`, `list_documents`, `merge_three_way`, `ai_request(intent, context, target)`. Started lazily on first client call; killed on shutdown.

the VS Code extension. Hosts the tree view, diagnostics, code lenses, form webviews, Markdown preview, walkthrough, `@projectspec` chat participant, and merge editor wiring. Schema-driven from Phase 2.5 onwards.

the standalone web form (planned). Shares the sidecar; outside this SDD's detailed-design scope but listed here so the "one backend, many surfaces" invariant ([PVD §6](PVD.md)) is visible in the architecture.

flow.intro: End-to-end authoring flow (HLR addition shown; LLRs, tests, modules, and merge resolution follow the same shape):
flow.step: The user opens `doc/Project.xml` in VS Code. The extension spawns `tools/project_io.py` and calls `parse_to_json` plus `list_documents` once on activation.
The schema-driven tree provider walks the hint registry returned by `parse_to_json` and contributes one root node per `ui:treeNode`-marked element kind, populated from the parsed payload.
The user clicks "Add HLR" on the HLRs tree node. The extension opens a form webview whose JSON Schema was derived from the relevant XSD subtree plus its `ui:form` hints.

On submit, the webview posts a JSON Patch to the extension, which forwards it to the sidecar's `apply_edit` method. The sidecar applies the patch on a working copy, runs XSD + lint, and (on success) writes the result back to `Project.xml` preserving comments and CDATA via `lxml`.
The extension's file watcher fires on the write; the tree, diagnostics, and code lenses refresh from a fresh `parse_to_json` call.
If `projectXml.previewOnSave` is enabled, the extension calls the sidecar's `render(document_id)` for the affected document and updates the side-by-side Markdown preview pane.

On commit + push + merge, if Git produces a conflict on `doc/Project.xml`, the extension offers `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts`, pulls `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs via `git show`, and calls the sidecar's `merge_three_way` (Stage A). Residual conflicts are routed to the AI pipeline (Stage B) and surfaced in VS Code's three-way merge editor.

design_goals.goal: `Project.xml` is the only authoritative artefact. Generated Markdown documents are an output, never an input. No design element, requirement, or test exists in any other store. From [PVD §6 Principle 1](PVD.md).

Inputs and outputs are text files in the repository. No database, no server, no binary store, no proprietary format. This rules out any feature that would require a runtime service to read the spec. From [PVD §6 Principle 2](PVD.md).

Every payload field is described in `tools/project.xsd` and documented in `Schema_Reference.md` before any template, renderer, or UI consumes it. `schema_version` is bumped on breaking changes. From [PVD §6 Principle 3](PVD.md).

The core renderer and linter use only the Python standard library plus Jinja2; XSD validation falls back gracefully when `lxml` and `xmllint` are absent. No heavy dependencies on the spec-generation hot path. From [PVD §6 Principle 4](PVD.md).

CLI, JSON-RPC sidecar, VS Code extension, web form, and AI assistance all call the same Python functions — directly or via the sidecar. UI layers never re-implement parsing, rendering, linting, or merging. From [PVD §6 Principle 5](PVD.md).

goal.name: No hand-written XML on the critical path

design_goals.goal: Routine authoring is doable end-to-end through the extension's structured surfaces. Any workflow that *requires* the user to edit XML by hand to perform a common task is a bug. From [PVD §6 Principle 6](PVD.md).

goal.name: AI as a co-author, not an oracle

design_goals.goal: AI-generated content is grounded in project data, constrained by typed JSON response schemas, and gated on the same XSD + lint pipeline as manual edits. Every AI write is diff-previewed and logged to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl`. The linter, not the model, is the authority on correctness. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md).

Every broken trace, duplicate ID, or unverified requirement is surfaced by the linter and (in-editor) by a diagnostic. Coverage gaps are explicit rows in the Traceability Matrix. Warnings are never downgraded to keep CI green. From [PVD §6 Principle 8](PVD.md).

`HLR-NNN` and `LLR-XXX-NN` IDs are contracts. They are never renumbered; new IDs take the next free number. Stage A merges honour this when allocating ids to newly-added items on collision. From [PVD §6 Principle 9](PVD.md).
Every behaviour worth describing is captured as an HLR/LLR with at least one bound test. The Traceability Matrix is the contract, not a status report. From [PVD §6 Principle 10](PVD.md).

Adding a new generated document, a new payload section, or a new field is a schema-and-template change — not a TypeScript change. The extension discovers what to render from `tools/project.xsd` UI hints and `<metadata><document>` entries. Bespoke visualisations and domain-specific lint rules are the only payload-aware code paths. From [PVD §6 Principle 11](PVD.md), implemented in SDP Phase 2.5.

Every optional capability fails closed: AI surfaces hide when no language model is available, XSD validation falls back to `xmllint` then to a structural-only pass with a note when `lxml` is absent, and the structured merger refuses rather than guesses when the Git merge base is unavailable. The deterministic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, code lenses, form panels, render, Stage A merge) keep working in every degraded mode. From [PVD §7.1](PVD.md) graceful-degradation contract.

No AI write lands without a diff preview; no merge resolution lands without the user driving the merge editor; every AI-authored edit is logged to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl`; every write goes through the same backup pipeline as a manual edit. "Undo last AI edit" is one click. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md) and the `Trust, transparency, and undo" requirements throughout PVD §5.6 and §5.7.

Grounding bundles never include `.git`, `node_modules`, or any file outside `doc/` and `tools/templates/` by default. AI surfaces are off in untrusted workspaces. The `projectXml.ai.contextAllowList` setting is the only knob that widens the disclosure surface. From [PVD §6 Principle 7](PVD.md) and the trusted-workspace gating called out in [SDP Phase 5](SDP.md).

module.purpose:
is the canonical schema for `doc/Project.xml`: every payload element, attribute, and (from Phase 2.5) the UI-hint vocabulary that drives the schema-driven extension surfaces.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1) for the payload schema. UI-hint `xs:appinfo` annotations land in Phase 2.5 per [SDP](SDP.md); the element catalogue and validation contract documented here are current.
module.responsibility: Constrain the structure of `<project>` and every payload (`<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, `<tests>`, plus future schema-declared sections).

Carry UI hints in `xs:appinfo` under the `https://tracer.dev/ui/1` namespace: `ui:treeNode`, `ui:form`, `ui:lens`, `ui:document`. The sidecar distils these into the hint registry consumed by the extension.
Be loadable by `lxml`, `xmllint`, and `xml.etree`. The linter detects and reports hint-vocabulary violations; missing UI hints are warnings, not errors.

interfaces.interface: `tools/render_doc.py` does not consume the XSD directly; it relies on the linter to have validated the document before render. Schema-shape changes that templates depend on require a coordinated template + `render_doc.py` update.

`tools/lint_project.py` validates `Project.xml` against the XSD using `lxml` (preferred) or `xmllint` (fallback), and gracefully degrades to "not validated" with a note when neither is available. UI-hint validation is additional and runs after structural validation succeeds.

`tools/project_io.py` parses the XSD on startup, extracts the UI-hint registry, caches it on the `parse_to_json` response (under `ui_hints_index`), and re-derives a JSON Schema for each form-target subtree on demand.

dependencies.dep: None at runtime; this is a static schema file.
Authoring depends on `xmllint` for local validation; `Schema_Reference.md` is the human-facing reference.

module.purpose:
is the document renderer: it turns `doc/Project.xml` plus a Jinja2 template into one Markdown spec document.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1). CLI, `--init` bootstrap, and the template data-surface (cross-reference indexes, coverage gap lists, `gh_slug` filter) are all shipping.
module.responsibility: Parse `Project.xml` into a `SimpleNamespace` tree (the `project.*` namespace consumed by every template).

Compute derived projections used by templates: flat lists (`flat_hlrs`, `flat_llrs`, `flat_tests`), id lookups (`hlr_by_id`, `llr_by_id`, `file_of_test`), cross-reference indexes (`hlrs_by_sdd`, `llrs_by_hlr`, `tests_by_hlr`, `tests_by_llr`), coverage-gap lists, and template filters (`gh_slug`).
Render any template against the `<metadata><document>` entry selected by CLI argument; the template owns all document-shape decisions (headings, tables, numbering).

Provide an importable library API (`render_to_str(template, doc_id, project_xml)`, `parse_project_to_dict(project_xml)`) used by the sidecar so the same code path is used by CLI, extension, web form, and AI pipeline.
Provide an `--init` mode that bootstraps a new project's `Project.xml` and `PVD.md` from skeletons.

interfaces.interface: `python3 tools/render_doc.py <template_path> <document_id> [--out <path>]` — render one document. `python3 tools/render_doc.py --init` — bootstrap.

`render_to_str(template_path: Path, document_id: str, project_xml: Path) -> str` — render to a string. `parse_project_to_dict(project_xml: Path) -> dict` — return the raw parsed tree (used by `project_merge.py` and the sidecar's JSON projection). Raises `ProjectXmlError` on any parse / template / metadata error; the CLI converts these to exit codes, library callers catch them directly.

module.purpose:
is the structural and semantic linter for `Project.xml`. Its findings drive both CI and the in-editor diagnostics surface.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1). Stable `Finding.code` values are emitted today; the Phase 2.5 work is to tighten the code set that the extension's Quick Fix table keys on.
module.responsibility: Validate well-formedness and XSD conformance against `tools/project.xsd`, using `lxml` (preferred), then `xmllint` (fallback), then a structural-only pass with a "not XSD-validated" note.

Check `<metadata>` shape: every template under `tools/templates/` must have a matching `<document id="…">`; document ids are unique. From Phase 2.5 the required-set is derived from templates, not a hard-coded list.
Check ID format and uniqueness for HLRs (`HLR-NNN`), LLRs (`LLR-XXX-NN`), and test names (free-form but unique within their `<file>`).
Resolve every `<trace>` reference; report broken refs as errors, weak refs (e.g. SDD section numbers that look malformed) as warnings.
Compute coverage gaps: HLRs with no LLR or test linking to them; LLRs with no test linking to them. Report as warnings; the Traceability Matrix template renders them as explicit rows.
Provide an importable `lint(project_xml: Path) -> LintResult` library API; the CLI is a thin wrapper.

interfaces.interface: `python3 tools/lint_project.py [--xml doc/Project.xml]` — prints findings to stdout / stderr; exits non-zero on errors.

`lint(project_xml: Path) -> LintResult` where `LintResult = { errors: list[Finding], warnings: list[Finding], notes: list[Finding], ok: bool }` and each `Finding` carries `message`, `line`, `column`, `xpath`, `code`. The `code` is stable and used by the extension to attach the right Quick Fix.

module.purpose:
holds the per-document Jinja2 templates that own all spec-doc scaffolding (titles, headings, numbering, tables, anchors).
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1). All five generated documents (`SDD`, `HLRs`, `LLRs`, `STP`, `Traceability`) plus the `PVD.md.template` bootstrap are present.
module.responsibility: One template per `<metadata><document>` entry. Each consumes the `project.*` namespace exposed by `render_doc.py` and emits Markdown.
Emit anchor `` tags immediately before every `HLR-NNN`, `LLR-XXX-NN`, and `test_…` row so the Traceability template can link to them.
Never invent payload fields. Adding a new field requires the schema, the renderer, and the template to be updated together.

interfaces.interface: `SDD.md.j2`, `HLRs.md.j2`, `LLRs.md.j2`, `STP.md.j2`, `Traceability.md.j2`. New documents add a sibling template plus a `<metadata><document id="…">` entry; from Phase 2.5 the extension picks them up automatically.
`PVD.md.template` is consumed by `render_doc.py --init` to seed `doc/PVD.md` for new projects.

dependencies.dep: The data surface exposed by `tools/render_doc.py` (see its module above).

module.title: Developer and CI convenience targets
module.purpose:
is the developer- and CI-facing wrapper around the toolchain documented in [SDP §0](SDP.md). It auto-detects the host OS, installs prerequisites, bootstraps a project venv, builds the VS Code extension, and runs the umbrella `ci` target (`lint` + `validate-xml` + `render` + `test` + `ext`).
**Status:** as-built. Targets exercised in CI keep the generated documents, the linter, the renderer, the test suite, and the VS Code extension build all passing on every commit.
module.responsibility: Detect the host OS family from `uname -s` and `/etc/os-release` (`debian`, `fedora`, `arch`, `macos`, `unknown`) and dispatch to the matching `prereqs-*` recipe.
Provide a slim `prereqs-ci` variant that omits VS Code, `vsce`, and `gh` for headless CI runners.
Auto-detect privilege escalation (`SUDO` is empty when already root, otherwise `sudo`) so the same recipes work in containerised CI and on a developer workstation.
Bootstrap a per-project venv, install `jinja2`/`lxml`/`pytest`/`xmlschema`, run `npm install` in the extension directory, and install the `redhat.vscode-xml` extension when `code` is on `PATH`.
Expose `lint`, `validate-xml`, `render`, `test`, `ext-typecheck`, `ext-build`, `ext-package`, and the `ci` umbrella as composable targets reusable by GitHub Actions and by humans.
Provide `clean`, `clean-docs`, `clean-ext`, and `distclean` for reversible removal of generated docs, extension build output, `__pycache__`, and the venv.

Self-verify TraceR's own spec stack: the `ci` target shall run lint, render every generated document, and run the pytest suite against TraceR's own `doc/Project.xml` so the repository's own specification artefacts are guaranteed lint-clean and in sync on every commit. A non-zero exit blocks merge.

interfaces.interface: `make -C tools detect`, `make -C tools prereqs` (developer), `make -C tools prereqs-ci` (CI), `make -C tools verify`, `make -C tools bootstrap`.
`make -C tools lint`, `make -C tools validate-xml`, `make -C tools render`, `make -C tools test`, `make -C tools ci` (lint + validate-xml + render + test + ext, fail-fast).
`make -C tools ext-typecheck`, `make -C tools ext-build`, `make -C tools ext` (alias), `make -C tools ext-package` (produces `.vsix` via `vsce`).
`make -C tools clean`, `make -C tools clean-docs`, `make -C tools clean-ext`, `make -C tools distclean`.

module.purpose:
is the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 sidecar that exposes every parse / render / lint / merge / AI operation to all UI surfaces. The "one backend, many surfaces" guarantee ([PVD §6 Principle 5](PVD.md)) is enforced here.
**Status:** Phase 1 ships `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, and `init_project` as JSON-RPC methods over line-delimited stdio. `apply_edit`, `list_documents`, `merge_three_way`, `ai_request`, and `subscribe_changes` are designed below but not yet implemented; they land in Phases 2.5–5.5 per [SDP](SDP.md).
module.responsibility: Speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout. Methods: `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `apply_edit`, `init_project`, `list_documents`, `merge_three_way`, `ai_request`, `subscribe_changes`, `shutdown`.

Be the only writer to `Project.xml` (via `apply_edit`); UI surfaces send JSON Patch ops, the sidecar applies them on the parsed tree, runs XSD + lint, and serializes back via `lxml` so that comments, CDATA, attribute order, and whitespace are preserved.
Be process-safe: started lazily on first client call, killed on `shutdown` or extension deactivate; survives a single failed request without crashing the session.

interfaces.interface: `render(document_id: str) -> { markdown, source_template }` — renders one document. The Markdown preview surface calls this; it never writes a file.

`parse_to_json() -> { project: ParsedNode, ui_hints_index, metadata, counts }` — generic projection of the whole tree plus the hint registry. The schema-driven tree, lens, and locator providers consume this exclusively.

`apply_edit(patch: JsonPatch, expect_clean: bool = true) -> { ok, lint, residual_diff }` — atomically apply, validate, write. Refuses if `expect_clean` is true and the in-editor text buffer is dirty (the extension prompts the user to save or discard).
`init_project(name, short_name, author) -> { paths_written }` — wraps `render_doc.py --init`.
`list_documents() -> [{ id, title, source, template, ui_document }]` — enumerates `<metadata><document>` entries; the extension's "Render <Doc>" command palette contributions are derived from this.

`ai_request(intent: str, context: dict, target: dict) -> { patch?, suggestion?, validations: [Finding], retries }` — delegates to `tools/ai/pipeline.py`. Used by the chat participant, the right-click "with AI" actions, and the merge resolver's Stage B.
`subscribe_changes() -> stream` — pushes notifications when the file watcher detects an out-of-band change to `Project.xml`. The extension uses this to refresh the tree.

error_handling.case: Returns a JSON-RPC error with `code = -32001` and the line/column of the failure; the extension surfaces it as a top-level diagnostic on the file.

`apply_edit` is serialised per session. A concurrent edit landing during validation causes the patch to be rebased on the new tree and re-validated; if rebase fails, the call returns `code = -32010` ("conflicting concurrent edit") and the caller retries.
`ai_request` returns `code = -32020` ("no language model available"); the extension hides the AI surfaces gracefully per [PVD §7.1](PVD.md) graceful-degradation contract.

module.title: Structured three-way merger (planned)
module.purpose:
is the deterministic three-way structural merger over `Project.xml` (Stage A of the merge pipeline described in [SDP Phase 5.5](SDP.md)).
**Status:** planned (Phase 5.5). No file ships in the current checkout; the design below freezes the contract the sidecar's `merge_three_way` will satisfy.
module.responsibility: Re-key elements by their stable ids (`HLR-NNN`, `LLR-XXX-NN`, test names, module paths) so a merge is position-independent.
Union additions when ids do not collide; on collision where both sides are new, allocate the next free id to one side (existing ids never move, per [PVD §6 Principle 9](PVD.md)).
Union `<traces>` entries by `(target, ref)` tuple, deduping.
Recompute `<metadata>/<counts>` from the merged tree.
Take the structurally-equivalent side when whitespace, comment, or attribute-order differences are the only divergence.

Emit residual conflicts (genuinely overlapping body edits, divergent trace targets, ID renames, schema-version bumps) as a structured list rather than fixing them; the AI pipeline (Stage B) consumes the list.
Refuse and report rather than guess when the merge base is unavailable (rebase-in-progress, octopus merges, cherry-picks without a base).

interfaces.interface: `merge(base: dict, ours: dict, theirs: dict) -> { merged: dict, residual_conflicts: [Conflict] }` where each input is the parsed-dict representation from `render_doc.parse_project_to_dict`. The merged tree is serialised through the same `lxml`-based write-back path as `apply_edit` so comments and CDATA are preserved.

dependencies.dep: `tools/lint_project.py` for the post-merge lint pass that gates acceptance.

module.title: AI authoring pipeline (planned)
module.purpose:
is the AI pipeline. It assembles a grounding bundle from project data, calls the language model with a typed JSON response schema, and validates the response through the same XSD + lint pipeline as manual edits.
**Status:** planned (Phase 5). No directory ships in the current checkout; the design below freezes the contract the sidecar's `ai_request` will satisfy.
module.responsibility: `context.py` — `build_ai_context(target) -> bundle` packs the schema subtree, `Schema_Reference.md` excerpt, PVD excerpt, SDD/HLR/LLR context appropriate to the intent, sibling items as style anchors, and the lint state of the target. A deterministic packer enforces `projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens`; the schema and the user intent are never dropped.

`pipeline.py` — implements the validate→retry loop: parse JSON against the intent's response schema, translate to a JSON Patch, apply on a copy of the tree, run XSD + `lint_project.lint`, and on failure retry with the findings as feedback. After max retries surface the suggestion + the failures to the user.

`intents/` — one Markdown file per intent, holding the system prompt and few-shot examples grounded in the schema. Authoring intents: `draft.hlr`, `draft.llr`, `draft.test`, `draft.module`, `draft.pvd`, `expand.hlr_to_llrs`, `expand.llr_to_tests`, `review.item`, `suggest.traces`, `gap.fix`. Merge intents: `merge.body`, `merge.trace`, `merge.rename`, `merge.schema_bump`.

**PVD ghostwriting flow** — `draft.pvd` differs from the other authoring intents in that the target document is hand-authored Markdown (`doc/PVD.md`), not a payload of `Project.xml`. The intent shall identify thin or missing sections (placeholders, single-sentence sections expected to be paragraphs, lists with one item where multiple are expected) by structure, surface targeted clarifying questions to the user before drafting any prose, and only then produce content matching the existing voice and heading style. The pipeline shall route accepted PVD edits through the same diff-preview gate as `Project.xml` edits and shall append the same provenance entry to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl`. Vision, scope, success metrics, and roadmap themes shall never be invented without an explicit user answer.
`schemas/` — one JSON Schema per intent describing the shape of a valid response (Pydantic-validated). The deterministic translator that maps the JSON to a JSON Patch lives next to each schema.
Append a provenance entry to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` per accepted/rejected suggestion (timestamp, intent, model, prompt hash, accept/reject, validator state).

interfaces.interface: `build_ai_context(target: TargetSpec) -> Bundle` (in `context.py`). `run(intent: str, context: Bundle, target: TargetSpec) -> AiResult` (in `pipeline.py`) — returns either an applied JSON Patch + lint result, or a rejected suggestion + the validator findings that blocked it.
The sidecar exposes `ai_request` (see project_io module above), which is the only entry point UI surfaces use; the TS side never imports `tools/ai/` directly.

dependencies.dep: `tools/project.xsd` and `Schema_Reference.md` for the grounding bundle's schema and authoring-guidance sections.
The host's language model (via the VS Code Language Model API on the TS side, never called directly from Python).

error_handling.case: Auto-retry with the parser error fed back as a correction prompt; counts against the configured retry budget.

Auto-retry with the new findings fed back. If the candidate introduces no *new* errors compared to the pre-edit state, it is accepted (an unrelated pre-existing warning does not block the suggestion).
Surface the original suggestion + the validator failures to the user instead of writing it; never silently apply.
Return an `AiResult` with `kind = "no-model"`. UI surfaces hide themselves; the linter, renderer, and Stage A merge keep working unchanged.

module.purpose:
is the first-class VS Code extension that turns `Project.xml` into a structured editing surface and is the primary delivery vehicle for the in-editor authoring, schema-driven views, AI assistance, and AI-mediated merge resolution called out in [PVD §5 / §7.1](PVD.md).
**Status:** Phase 1 ships the activation scaffolding, sidecar wrapper (`src/sidecar.ts`), `Project Spec` tree view, lint diagnostics, and the `revealInXml` command. Schema-driven surfaces, form webviews, AI surfaces, walkthrough, and merge integration land in Phases 2.5–5.5 per [SDP](SDP.md) and [tools/PLAN_vscode_extension.md](../tools/PLAN_vscode_extension.md).
module.responsibility: Activate on workspaces containing `doc/Project.xml`. Spawn `tools/project_io.py` once per session and route every operation through it; never parse, render, lint, or merge `Project.xml` itself.

Contribute the "Project Spec" Activity Bar view, the Markdown preview pane, the form webviews, the Walkthrough, the `@projectspec` chat participant, the merge editor integration, and the status bar item.
From Phase 2.5 onwards, build all generic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, lenses, locator, render commands) at runtime from the `ui_hints_index` and `<metadata><document>` list returned by the sidecar.
Declare `extensionDependencies` on `redhat.vscode-xml` so the user gets XSD-backed XML editing (syntax, outline, completion) for free.
Contribute every `projectXml.*` setting through `contributes.configuration` (see Data Dictionary §Settings for the authoritative list and defaults).

Be `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"`: AI surfaces are off until the workspace is trusted; the deterministic surfaces (tree, diagnostics, lenses, forms, render, Stage A merge) keep working in untrusted mode.

interfaces.interface: `workspaceContains:doc/Project.xml`, `onLanguage:xml` (filtered to `Project.xml`), and the `onCommand:projectXml.*` family.

TypeScript, `@vscode/extension` API, esbuild for bundling, mocha + `@vscode/test-electron` for tests. Webviews use React + react-jsonschema-form for form panels; the bundle is shared with the planned web form to avoid duplication.

The host's Language Model API (`vscode.lm.selectChatModels`) for AI surfaces; absent implies graceful degradation.

module.title: Project Spec tree view
module.purpose:
contributes the "Project Spec" Activity Bar view that gives every payload a structured outline with inline status badges. From Phase 2.5 it is built entirely from the schema's UI hints, with no per-payload TypeScript.
**Status:** Phase 1 ships a payload-aware `ProjectSpecProvider` rooted at `doc/Project.xml`. The schema-driven hint walk, status badges, and AI context-menu commands described below are the Phase 2.5–5 target.
module.responsibility: Walk `ui_hints_index.treeNodes` and emit one root node per `ui:treeNode`-marked element kind, populated from the parsed payload returned by `parse_to_json`.
Annotate each node with a count badge and surface lint- derived status badges (`⚠`, `❌`) on items with coverage gaps or broken refs.

Provide context-menu commands: `Edit`, `Reveal in XML`, `Add child …`, `Delete`, `Render this section`, `Draft / Expand / Review with AI`. The set of available commands per node is derived from the hint registry, not hard-coded per element kind.
Locate elements in the underlying XML for `Reveal in XML` via the generic locator (`util/locator.ts`), which takes `(elementName, idAttr, idValue)` from the hint registry.

interfaces.interface: `projectXml.tree` registered against the `projectXml-explorer` view container in `contributes.viewsContainers`.
Subscribes to `projectXml.fileChanged` (workspace file watcher on `doc/Project.xml`) and to the sidecar's `subscribe_changes` stream; debounced refresh.

module.title: Diagnostics and Quick Fixes
module.purpose:
mirrors lint findings into the Problems panel as VS Code `Diagnostic` objects, with payload-agnostic Quick Fixes for the most common findings.
**Status:** Phase 1 ships `LintDiagnosticsProvider`, which mirrors lint findings into the Problems panel. The `CodeActionProvider` Quick Fix table below is the Phase 2.5 target; the AI-suggest variants land with Phase 5.
module.responsibility: Translate each lint `Finding` to a `Diagnostic` using the xpath/line/column carried by the finding; preserve the finding's stable `code` so Quick Fixes can target it.

Provide a `CodeActionProvider` whose Quick Fixes are table-driven from the finding's `code`: "Replace ref with…" picker for broken-trace findings, "Renumber as …" for ID-format errors, "Insert standard `<document>` row" for missing-document warnings, "Create stub test entry" for missing-test warnings, plus an "AI: suggest correct ref" fix on broken-trace findings when AI is enabled.

interfaces.interface: `projectXml-lint` collection; cleared and rebuilt on each lint pass.
Registered for `language: xml` filtered to `Project.xml`. Returns the union of generic + AI fixes that apply to the findings on the requested range.

dependencies.dep: Sidecar `apply_edit` (Quick Fixes apply through the same write path as form edits).
The AI participant module (for the AI-suggest variant of each fix).

module.title: Sidecar JSON-RPC client (TypeScript)
module.purpose:
is the long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 client that every extension surface uses to talk to `tools/project_io.py`. It is the only TypeScript code that ever spawns a Python process; the surfaces never call out to a child process themselves.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1). Wraps `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, and `init_project`; `apply_edit`, `merge_three_way`, and `ai_request` are added as the matching Python methods land in Phases 2.5–5.5.
module.responsibility: Spawn `tools/project_io.py` lazily on first call, with the interpreter chosen by `util/paths.getProjectIoScript` (honouring `projectXml.pythonPath`).
Frame requests as line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; correlate responses by numeric id; surface errors as `SidecarError(code, message)`.
Tear the process down on `dispose()` (extension deactivate); buffer in-flight requests so a single bad request does not crash the session.
Stream the sidecar's stderr to a dedicated VS Code `OutputChannel` so the user can diagnose interpreter problems without leaving the editor.

interfaces.interface: `new ProjectIoClient(outputChannel)`; `lint()`, `render({ template, metadata_id })`, `parseToJson()`, `initProject({...})`; `dispose()`. Every method returns a typed Promise; rejections carry a `SidecarError` with the JSON-RPC error code.

module.title: Command palette contributions
module.purpose:
hosts the per-command modules wired into VS Code's command palette through `package.json`'s `contributes.commands`. Each command is a thin handler that delegates to the sidecar and updates the relevant view.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1) for `projectXml.refresh`, `projectXml.lint`, and `projectXml.revealInXml`. The schema-driven `Add child …`, `Render this section …`, and AI-mediated commands land in Phases 2.5–5 alongside the views that call them.
module.responsibility: `revealInXml.ts` — open `doc/Project.xml`, locate the selected payload element via `util/locator.ts`, and reveal its line in the active editor. Used by the tree view's context menu and (later) by the code-lens action.
Each command is registered in `extension.ts`'s `activate` function and disposed of when the extension deactivates. Commands never reach into provider internals; they go through the sidecar.

interfaces.interface: `projectXml.refresh` (re-runs `parse_to_json` and rebuilds the tree), `projectXml.lint` (re-runs lint and refreshes diagnostics), `projectXml.revealInXml` (jumps to a payload element from the tree).

module.title: Shared helpers (paths, locator)
module.purpose:
is the small library of payload-agnostic helpers shared by every other extension module: workspace path discovery, interpreter selection, and element location inside `doc/Project.xml`.
**Status:** as-built (Phase 1). The locator is currently seeded with a hard-coded payload-element table; from Phase 2.5 it is regenerated at runtime from `ui_hints_index` so it gains new payloads without TypeScript changes.
module.responsibility: `paths.ts` — resolve `doc/Project.xml`, the tools directory, and the Python interpreter from the active workspace and `projectXml.*` settings; surface `describeWorkspaceState()` for the sidecar's startup diagnostics.

`locator.ts` — given an `(elementName, idAttr, idValue)` triple, scan the open `Project.xml` text buffer (or the on-disk file) and return a `vscode.Range` for the matching element. The single source of truth for "jump to element" across the tree, code lenses, and Quick Fixes.

interfaces.interface: `getProjectXmlPath()`, `getToolsDir()`, `getProjectIoScript()`, `getConfig()`, `describeWorkspaceState()`.
`locateElement(uri, { elementName, idAttr, idValue }) -> vscode.Range | undefined`.

dependencies.dep: The Microsoft Python extension's interpreter API (optional; falls back to `python3`/`python` on PATH).

module.title: Code lenses (planned)
module.purpose:
decorates schema-marked elements in `Project.xml` with inline status and click-through actions.
**Status:** planned (Phase 2). No directory ships in the current checkout; the design below freezes the contract.
module.responsibility: Walk `ui_hints_index.lenses` and attach the named lens kind (`coverage`, `tracesCount`, custom) to every matching element. From Phase 2.5 the lens provider has zero hard-coded element selectors.
Render compact summaries (e.g. "3 LLRs · 5 tests" on an HLR) plus action lenses (`Edit`, `Preview section`, `🪄 AI`).
Resolve click targets through the generic locator so "jump to LLR-PCL-04" works for any schema-declared id attribute.

interfaces.interface: Registered for `language: xml` filtered to `Project.xml`. Lazily computes lens text from the cached `ui_hints_index` and the latest `parse_to_json` payload.

module.title: Form panels and Markdown preview (planned)
module.purpose:
hosts the single-item form webviews used to edit one payload element at a time, plus the side-by-side Markdown preview pane.
**Status:** planned (Phases 3–4). No directory ships in the current checkout; the design below freezes the contract shared with [tools/PLAN_web_form.md](../tools/PLAN_web_form.md).
module.responsibility: Open one form panel per `Edit`/`Add` action. The form's JSON Schema comes from the sidecar's `parse_to_json` response, which derives it from the relevant XSD subtree plus per-field `ui:form` hints.
On submit, post a JSON Patch to the extension which forwards it to `apply_edit`. On `apply_edit` returning a clean lint, the extension closes the panel and refreshes the tree.
Handle dirty-buffer collisions: if `Project.xml` is open in a text editor with unsaved changes, prompt the user to save or discard before applying the patch.
Render the Markdown preview by calling sidecar `render` for the affected document and writing the result to a virtual document; honour `projectXml.previewOnSave`.
Expose a "Draft this field with AI" button next to long Markdown fields; the AI insertion goes into the field, not straight to disk.

interfaces.interface: `form.ready`, `form.submit`, `form.cancel`, `form.aiDraftField`. Bundle is React + RJSF; built once and shared with the planned web form (PLAN_web_form.md).
Uses VS Code's built-in Markdown preview command (`markdown.showPreviewToSide`) against a virtual `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` URI served by an in-memory content provider.

module.title: Guided authoring (Walkthrough) (planned)
module.purpose:
contributes the VS Code Walkthrough that steps a new user through bootstrapping a project and filling each payload in order. The IDE-native equivalent of the web form's wizard.
**Status:** planned (Phase 4). No directory ships in the current checkout.
module.responsibility: Provide seven steps: bootstrap, PVD, SDD, HLRs, LLRs, tests, render & commit. Each step has Markdown content, a "Run command" link, and an automatic completion check (usually file-state or count-based).
Each step's "Run command" link can optionally be "Run command with AI", which pre-drafts the section through the authoring intents (Phase 5) rather than opening an empty form.

interfaces.interface: Registered under `contributes.walkthroughs` in the extension's `package.json`. Step IDs are stable so VS Code can persist completion state across sessions.

dependencies.dep: All command modules under `commands/` (each step ends in a command invocation).
The AI participant module (for the "with AI" variants).

module.title: AI participant and merge surface (planned)
module.purpose:
hosts the `@projectspec` chat participant, the right-click "with AI" actions, and the merge editor integration. The TypeScript side of the AI pipeline; the heavy lifting lives in `tools/ai/`.
**Status:** planned (Phase 5). No directory ships in the current checkout.
module.responsibility: Register the chat participant via `vscode.chat.createChatParticipant` with the `/draft-hlr`, `/expand`, `/review`, `/gap-fill`, and `/resolve-conflicts` slash commands.
Translate every chat / right-click / Quick Fix invocation into an `ai_request` call on the sidecar; surface the result through a diff preview before any write.

Detect a conflicted `doc/Project.xml` via the `git` extension API; expose `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts`; pull `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs via `git show`; call the sidecar's `merge_three_way`; open the result in VS Code's three-way merge editor with each AI-resolved region badged "✨ AI suggestion".

Honour `projectXml.ai.enabled`, `projectXml.merge.enabled`, and `projectXml.merge.aiResidualResolution`; the last must be forced off when `ai.enabled` is false. Hide every AI surface cleanly when `vscode.lm.selectChatModels` returns no models.
Never auto-apply: the diff preview (for authoring) and the merge editor (for merge resolution) are the only commit surfaces.

Appends one entry per AI-resolved region or per authoring suggestion to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` (timestamp, intent, model, prompt hash, accept/reject, validator state).

`untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` blocks AI activation; a warning notification explains the gating once per session.
The merge resolver refuses with a notification ("Stage A requires the Git merge base; falling back to manual resolution") rather than silently picking one side.

introduction.purpose:
This document is the Software Test Plan (STP) for **TraceR**. It describes how the Python core (the renderer, linter, and JSON-RPC sidecar) and the Phase 1-2 VS Code extension surfaces (sidecar client, tree view, lint diagnostics, reveal-in-XML, code lenses, render & preview) are verified, names the framework and tooling, and fixes the convention by which every test traces back to the LLRs and HLRs it covers.
The STP itself is rendered from `<stp>` and `<tests>` payloads in [doc/Project.xml](Project.xml). The Test Catalogue (§3) and the LLR Coverage Matrix (§4) are computed by the template directly from `<tests>` and `<llrs>` and so always reflect the current source of truth.
introduction.scope:
Verification scope tracks the SDP phases that have shipped:
* Phase 0 — JSON-RPC sidecar (`tools/project_io.py`). * Phase 1 — read-only VS Code extension surfaces (sidecar client, Project Spec tree view, lint diagnostics, reveal-in-XML). * Phase 2 — coverage code lenses, virtual-document Markdown preview, and the `renderAndPreview` / `renderAll` commands.
Unshipped phases (form panels, walkthrough, AI authoring, structured merge) are deliberately out of scope; their HLRs surface as coverage gaps in [Traceability.md](Traceability.md) until the relevant SDP phase lands.

related.doc: [PVD.md](PVD.md) — product vision and success metrics that the STP exists to make measurable.
[SDD.md](SDD.md) — module decomposition and design intent that the LLRs codify.
[HLRs.md](HLRs.md) — high-level requirements that every test ultimately traces back to.
[LLRs.md](LLRs.md) — function-level `shall` clauses that individual tests verify.
[Traceability.md](Traceability.md) — forward and reverse matrices computed from the same `<traces>` data this STP uses.
[Schema_Reference.md](Schema_Reference.md) — the contract between `Project.xml`, the renderer, and the templates.

level.name: Unit
level.style: White-box, per-module; one `TestCase` class per surface, one method per `shall` clause.

level.name: Integration (subprocess)
level.style: Black-box; drives the real sidecar over stdin/stdout exactly as the VS Code extension does.

level.name: Cross-surface equivalence
level.driver: Python `unittest` comparing in-process and subprocess paths
level.style: Pinning test asserting the CLI, the in-process library, and the JSON-RPC sidecar return byte-identical findings for the same input.

level.name: Unit (TypeScript, tier-1)
level.driver: Mocha + ts-node (`npm run test:unit`) with a hand-rolled `vscode` API mock
level.style: Pure-Node unit tests for the extension modules that do not require a VS Code host — path resolution, document locator regexes, the BASELINE_DOCUMENTS constant, and the JSON-RPC line-framing in ProjectIoClient. Stays inside the minimal-deps envelope (HLR-046); no @vscode/test-electron download.

level.name: Static
level.style: Schema validation, ID format/uniqueness, trace resolution, coverage-gap reporting; treated as a verification step that runs in CI alongside the unit suite.

strategy.framework:
The Python verification path uses the standard-library `unittest` package — no `pytest`, no third-party Python test runner, no plugins. The TypeScript tier-1 path uses `mocha` + `ts-node` with a hand-rolled `vscode` API mock so the extension's headless modules load in plain Node without a VS Code host. Both paths stay inside the same minimal-dependency envelope (HLR-046) that the production code respects: a fresh checkout can run the full Python suite with only `python3` plus `jinja2` installed, and the TypeScript suite with only `npm install` in `tools/vscode-project-xml/`.
Tests are organised one `TestCase` (Python) or `describe` block (TypeScript) per public surface, and one method / `it` per `shall` clause; method names mirror the LLR mnemonic where practical (e.g. `test_render_hlrs_returns_markdown_with_single_trailing_newline` verifies LLR-RND-03). Temporary `Project.xml` skeletons are minted via `render_doc.init_project` so each test runs against a known-good baseline rather than the repo's evolving `doc/Project.xml`.

build_execution.intro: The full suite is run from the repository root with the standard `unittest` discovery invocation:
build_execution.step: `python3 -m unittest discover -s test -v` — discovers every `test_*.py` module under [test/](../test/), instantiates each `TestCase` class, and runs every `test_*` method.

`python3 tools/lint_project.py --xml doc/Project.xml --xsd tools/project.xsd` — runs the static verification step on the repo's own `Project.xml`. CI treats a non-zero exit code (i.e. any *error* finding) as a build failure; warnings are surfaced but do not break the build (HLR-014, HLR-042).
`(cd tools/vscode-project-xml && npm run compile && npm run build)` — type-checks the VS Code extension with `tsc --noEmit` and bundles it with `esbuild`; failure of either step is a build failure.

`(cd tools/vscode-project-xml && npm run test:unit)` — runs the Mocha + ts-node tier-1 unit suite for the extension modules that do not require a VS Code host (path resolution, locator regexes, baseline-documents catalogue, JSON-RPC line-framing). Failure is a build failure.
build_execution.outro: The unit suite must complete with zero failures and zero errors before a change is considered mergeable; the linter must complete with zero error findings (warnings tracked but not blocking); the extension build must complete with no TypeScript or esbuild errors.

pass_fail.criterion: **Unit suite.** `python3 -m unittest discover -s test` reports `OK` with zero failures and zero errors. A single failing assertion blocks the build.

**Lint.** `python3 tools/lint_project.py` exits 0 (zero *error* findings). Warnings — including coverage gaps for HLRs whose implementation has not yet shipped — are recorded in the Problems panel and the rendered Traceability Matrix but are not blocking.

**Cross-surface equivalence.** `test_lint_matches_cli_findings` and `test_subprocess_lint_matches_in_process_lint` must both pass; they pin HLR-043 (cross-surface output equivalence) by asserting that the CLI, the in-process library, and the JSON-RPC sidecar produce byte-identical findings for the same `Project.xml`.
**Extension build.** `npm run compile` (TypeScript strict-mode type-check) and `npm run build` (esbuild bundle) both exit 0 in [tools/vscode-project-xml/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/).

**Smoke against the real repo.** `test_real_repo_project_xml_lints` and the `_matches_*` pair both run against the live `doc/Project.xml`, so a regression in the linter, the renderer, or the sidecar that only manifests on the real corpus still trips the suite.

strategy.traceability_convention:
Every `test_*` method has a matching `<test name="…">` entry under `<tests>/<file path="…">` in [doc/Project.xml](Project.xml). Each `<test>` carries one `<purpose>` paragraph (mirroring the docstring or inline comment that motivates the assertion) and one `<traces>` block with one `<trace target="LLR" ref="LLR-XXX-NN"/>` per LLR the test verifies, plus optional `<trace target="HLR" ref="HLR-NNN"/>` entries when the test pins a high-level requirement directly (typically the cross-surface equivalence and JSON-RPC contract tests).
The linter resolves every `ref` against the union of LLR / HLR ids and reports unknown references as errors; coverage gaps (LLRs or HLRs with no test claiming them) are reported as warnings and rendered in [Traceability.md §6](Traceability.md). To add a new test: write the `test_*` method, add the matching `<test>` entry under the right `<file>`, then re-render `STP.md` and `Traceability.md`.

integration_environment.intro: TraceR has no external runtime services to stand up — the renderer, the linter, and the sidecar are all pure-Python processes. The only integration surface that requires a real subprocess is the JSON-RPC sidecar itself, which the VS Code extension drives via stdin/stdout. The fixture below isolates that surface so the test suite covers the same wire path the extension uses.

artefact.label: Sidecar stdout (one JSON response per line)
Sidecar exit code (0 = clean shutdown on stdin EOF)

integration_environment.outro: The `bootstrapped_project_xml` fixture is reused by the renderer, linter, and sidecar tests so each suite runs against an isolated, known-good baseline rather than the repo's evolving `doc/Project.xml`. The handful of tests that *do* run against the live `doc/Project.xml` — `test_real_repo_project_xml_lints`, `test_lint_matches_cli_findings`, `test_subprocess_lint_matches_in_process_lint` — exist precisely to catch regressions that only surface on the real corpus.

tool.name: `python3` (3.10+)
tool.required_for: Running the renderer, linter, sidecar, and the unit suite
tool.notes: Standard library only on the verification path; no `pytest`, no `lxml` requirement.

tool.name: `jinja2`
tool.notes: Single third-party Python dependency (HLR-046). Pinned via the project's `requirements.txt` if present.

tool.name: `lxml` (optional)
tool.notes: When absent, `validate_structure` falls back to `xmllint`; when both are absent, it degrades to a well-formedness-only pass and emits an explicit note (LLR-VST-01..04).

tool.name: `xmllint` (optional)
tool.notes: Used when `lxml` is not importable. Available on most Linux distros via the `libxml2-utils` package; on macOS via Xcode CLT.

tool.name: `node` (18+) and `npm`
tool.required_for: Building the VS Code extension under [tools/vscode-project-xml/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/)
tool.notes: Required only to type-check and bundle the extension; the Python verification path does not depend on Node.

tool.name: `tsc` and `esbuild`
tool.required_for: Strict-mode TypeScript type-check and extension bundling
tool.notes: Invoked via `npm run compile` and `npm run build` respectively. Both must exit 0 for an extension change to be considered mergeable.

tool.name: `mocha` + `ts-node`
tool.notes: Invoked via `npm run test:unit`. Loads the extension source under a hand-rolled `vscode` API mock so no VS Code host is needed; the mock surface lives at [tools/vscode-project-xml/test/unit/__mocks__/vscode.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/test/unit/__mocks__/vscode.ts) and grows only as tier-1 coverage demands.

tool.name: VS Code 1.85+ with the `redhat.vscode-xml` extension
tool.required_for: Manual / acceptance verification of the Phase 1-2 extension surfaces (tree view, diagnostics, code lenses, virtual-doc preview)
tool.notes: Declared as `extensionDependencies` in the extension manifest (LLR-ACT-04). Tier-1 unit tests cover the headless logic (paths, locator, documents, JSON-RPC framing); UI behaviour (lens visibility, tree population, preview pane) remains a manual acceptance check until a Phase 5/6 `@vscode/test-electron` harness lands alongside the AI/merge surfaces.

stp.maintenance:
The STP and the test suite evolve together. When a new SDP phase lands:
1. **Add LLRs** for any new function or surface in `<llrs>` so the new code has a documented `shall` clause to verify against. 2. **Add tests** under [test/](../test/) — one `TestCase` per surface, one `test_*` method per `shall` clause — and add the matching `<test name="…">` entry under the appropriate `<file>` in `<tests>`. Cite at least one LLR (and optionally an HLR) in the `<traces>` block. 3. **Update `<stp>`** if the new phase introduces a new test level (e.g. UI automation against the extension host), a new fixture (e.g. a fake AI provider for Phase 5), or a new tool dependency. The strategy, fixture, and tooling sections are the only parts of the STP that need direct edits; the catalogue and matrix regenerate automatically. 4. **Re-render** the documents: `python3 tools/render_doc.py tools/templates/STP.md.j2 STP --out doc/STP.md` and the matching `Traceability.md` invocation. Run `python3 tools/lint_project.py` to confirm zero error findings.
Unshipped HLRs deliberately surface as coverage gaps in [Traceability.md §6](Traceability.md) until the relevant phase delivers tests against them — the gap list is the project's verification backlog.

section.title: Source of Truth and Schema
section.intro: Requirements covering the canonical XML store, the schema that constrains it, and the invariants every other component depends on. Map directly to [SDD §3](SDD.md#3) (the schema) and the foundational design goals in [SDD §2.2](SDD.md#22).

hlr.name: Single Source of Truth
hlr.text: The system shall maintain `doc/Project.xml` as the single authoritative store of every design element, requirement, and test, and shall treat all generated Markdown documents (`SDD.md`, `HLRs.md`, `LLRs.md`, `STP.md`, `Traceability.md`) as outputs that are never read back as inputs by any component.

hlr.name: Schema-Constrained Payloads
hlr.text: The system shall validate `doc/Project.xml` against `tools/project.xsd` before any render or write, and shall reject any payload that violates the schema's element, attribute, cardinality, or child-order constraints.

hlr.name: Schema Versioning
hlr.text: The schema shall expose a `schema_version` attribute on `<project>` and the system shall require this attribute to be incremented whenever a structural change is made that existing templates or `tools/render_doc.py` could not consume unchanged.

hlr.name: Schema-Driven UI Hints
hlr.text: The schema shall carry UI-hint annotations under the `https://tracer.dev/ui/1` namespace (`ui:treeNode`, `ui:form`, `ui:lens`, `ui:document`) and the sidecar shall publish these as a runtime hint registry that downstream surfaces consume without any per-payload TypeScript code.

hlr.name: Stable Identifiers
hlr.text: The system shall enforce `HLR-NNN` and `LLR-XXX-NN` identifier formats; the linter shall flag malformed IDs as errors and duplicate IDs as errors; allocation of new IDs shall always take the next free number so that existing IDs are never renumbered.

hlr.name: No Runtime Service Dependency
hlr.text: The product shall require no database, no network service, no binary store, and no proprietary file format to read, render, or verify a project's specification stack; every input and output shall be a plain text file under version control so that the spec stack is fully usable with `git`, `xmllint`, and a text editor and nothing else.

section.title: Document Rendering
section.intro: Requirements covering the renderer ([SDD §4](SDD.md#4)) and the Jinja2 template stack ([SDD §6](SDD.md#6)) that turns `Project.xml` into the five generated Markdown documents.

hlr.name: One Template per Generated Document
hlr.text: For each `<metadata><document id="…">` entry the system shall provide exactly one Jinja2 template under `tools/templates/` that owns the document's headings, numbering, and tables; the renderer shall select the template by document id at render time.

hlr.name: Template Data Surface
hlr.text: The renderer shall expose a stable `project.*` namespace to templates that includes the parsed payloads, flat lists (`flat_hlrs`, `flat_llrs`, `flat_tests`), id-based lookups (`hlr_by_id`, `llr_by_id`, `file_of_test`), and cross-reference indexes (`hlrs_by_sdd`, `llrs_by_hlr`, `tests_by_hlr`, `tests_by_llr`); templates shall not recompute these relations.

hlr.name: Renderer Library API
hlr.text: The renderer shall expose an importable library API (`render_to_str`, `parse_project_to_dict`) so the sidecar, the merger, and the AI pipeline can render and parse without spawning a subprocess; the CLI shall be a thin wrapper around this API.

hlr.name: Project Bootstrap
hlr.text: The renderer shall provide an `--init` mode that creates a skeleton `doc/Project.xml` and substitutes `tools/templates/PVD.md.template` into a new `doc/PVD.md`, allowing a fresh project to be set up in one command.

hlr.name: Template Anchor Convention
hlr.text: The HLRs, LLRs, and STP templates shall each emit `` anchors immediately before every `HLR-NNN`, `LLR-XXX-NN`, and `test_*` row so the Traceability template can produce stable cross-document links; payloads shall not embed anchors.

section.title: Linting and Traceability
section.intro: Requirements covering the linter ([SDD §5](SDD.md#5)) and the end-to-end traceability invariants it enforces.

hlr.name: XSD Validation Fallback Chain
hlr.text: The linter shall validate `doc/Project.xml` against `tools/project.xsd` using `lxml` when available, fall back to `xmllint` when it is not, and degrade to a structural-only pass with an explicit "not XSD-validated" note when neither is available; in every case the linter shall surface a clear note about which validator was used.

hlr.name: Stable Lint Codes
hlr.text: Every lint finding shall carry a stable `code` string (`broken-trace`, `id-format`, `no-test`, …) so the extension's Quick Fix table and downstream automation can attach behaviour to a finding by id rather than by message text.

hlr.name: Trace Reference Resolution
hlr.text: The linter shall resolve every `<trace target="…" ref="…"/>` reference and shall report unresolved or syntactically-malformed references as errors, and weakly-resolvable references (e.g. SDD section refs that look mis-formatted) as warnings.

hlr.name: Coverage-Gap Reporting
hlr.text: The linter shall compute coverage gaps — HLRs with no LLR or test linking to them, and LLRs with no test linking to them — and shall surface them as warnings; the Traceability template shall render them as explicit rows so gaps are never silently hidden.

hlr.name: Metadata Completeness
hlr.text: The linter shall verify that every Jinja2 template under `tools/templates/` has a matching `<metadata><document id="…">` entry and that document IDs are unique; missing or duplicate entries shall be reported as errors.

hlr.name: Warnings Are Never Silently Suppressed
hlr.text: The linter and every surface that consumes its findings shall treat warnings as first-class output: warnings shall not be downgraded to keep CI green, and any tool that aggregates findings (the Problems panel, the `ci` umbrella, the Traceability template's coverage-gap rows) shall display them verbatim. The only legitimate way to silence a finding is to fix the underlying issue or document the gap explicitly in `Traceability.md`.

section.title: JSON-RPC Sidecar
section.intro: Requirements covering the long-running sidecar ([SDD §8](SDD.md#8)) that is the only backend any UI surface calls into.

hlr.name: JSON-RPC Wire Contract
hlr.text: The sidecar shall speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over line-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout, shall correlate requests and responses by numeric `id`, and shall return errors as standard JSON-RPC error objects so any client (extension, web form, CI script) can interoperate with the same wire format.

hlr.name: One Backend, Many Surfaces
hlr.text: The sidecar shall be the only component that performs parsing, rendering, linting, structural merging, or AI requests; UI surfaces shall not re-implement any of these operations and shall route every call through the sidecar.

hlr.name: Whitespace-Preserving Writes
hlr.text: When the sidecar writes back to `doc/Project.xml` (via `apply_edit` or after a structural merge) it shall preserve comments, CDATA sections, attribute order, and whitespace so that diffs reflect the user's intent rather than the serializer's preferences.

hlr.name: Atomic Validate-then-Write
hlr.text: `apply_edit` shall apply each JSON Patch on a working copy of the parsed tree, run XSD plus lint validation, and only on success persist the result to `doc/Project.xml`; failures shall leave the on-disk file untouched and shall return the validation findings to the caller.

hlr.name: Cross-Surface Output Equivalence
hlr.text: For a given `doc/Project.xml`, the CLI, the JSON-RPC sidecar, the VS Code extension, and the planned web form shall return byte-identical lint findings (same `code`, severity, line, and column) and byte-identical rendered Markdown for every generated document; divergence between any two surfaces shall be a release-blocking defect.

section.title: VS Code Extension Authoring Surface
section.intro: Requirements covering the in-editor authoring surface ([SDD §11–§19](SDD.md#11)). The extension is the primary delivery vehicle for the "no hand-written XML on the critical path" goal in [SDD §2.2](SDD.md#22).

hlr.name: Extension Activation
hlr.text: The extension shall activate on workspaces containing `doc/Project.xml`, shall declare `redhat.vscode-xml` as an extension dependency so users get XSD-backed XML editing for free, and shall declare `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` so the deterministic surfaces remain available in untrusted workspaces while AI surfaces are gated off.

hlr.name: Sidecar Lifecycle
hlr.text: The extension shall spawn `tools/project_io.py` lazily on first call, shall correlate JSON-RPC responses by id, shall stream the sidecar's stderr to a dedicated VS Code `OutputChannel`, and shall tear the process down on extension deactivate.

hlr.name: Project Spec Tree View
hlr.text: The extension shall contribute a "Project Spec" Activity Bar view that renders one root node per payload kind, populated from the sidecar's `parse_to_json` response; from Phase 2.5 the contributed nodes shall be derived from the schema's UI-hint registry rather than from hard-coded TypeScript.

hlr.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel
hlr.text: The extension shall mirror every lint finding into VS Code's Problems panel as a `Diagnostic`, preserving the finding's stable `code`, line, column, and xpath so Quick Fixes, filters, and CI integrations can act on it.

hlr.name: Reveal in XML
hlr.text: The extension shall provide a `Reveal in Project.xml` command that, given an `(elementName, idAttr, idValue)` triple from any surface, opens `doc/Project.xml` and selects the matching element via the generic locator helper.

hlr.name: Quick Fixes for Common Findings
hlr.text: The extension shall provide payload-agnostic Quick Fixes for the most common lint findings (broken trace ref, malformed ID, missing-document metadata, missing-test gap), keyed on the finding's stable `code` so new fixes are added by table entry rather than per-payload code.

hlr.name: Structured Form Editing
hlr.text: The extension shall provide a form webview for every payload element kind whose JSON Schema is derived at runtime from the relevant XSD subtree plus per-field `ui:form` hints, so that adding a new field is a schema-and-hint change rather than a TypeScript change.

hlr.name: Side-by-Side Markdown Preview
hlr.text: The extension shall offer a side-by-side Markdown preview for each generated document, populated by calling the sidecar's `render` method against an in-memory virtual document so no preview ever writes to disk; the preview shall refresh on save when `projectXml.previewOnSave` is enabled.

hlr.name: Guided Authoring Walkthrough
hlr.text: The extension shall contribute a VS Code Walkthrough that steps a new user through bootstrap → PVD → SDD → HLRs → LLRs → tests → render & commit, with each step's completion check derived from the underlying file or count state rather than from a separately-maintained checklist.

section.title: AI Authoring Pipeline
section.intro: Requirements covering the AI co-author surface ([SDD §10](SDD.md#10) and [SDD §20](SDD.md#20)). Every requirement here is a Phase 5 deliverable in [SDP](SDP.md); the contracts are frozen now so the deterministic surfaces below them can be built without guessing how AI will plug in.

hlr.name: Grounded AI Requests
hlr.text: Every AI request shall include a deterministically-assembled grounding bundle (schema subtree, `Schema_Reference.md` excerpt, PVD excerpt, sibling items, current lint state of the target) capped by `projectXml.ai.maxContextTokens`; the schema and the user intent shall never be dropped by the packer when truncation is required.

hlr.name: Typed AI Responses
hlr.text: Every named AI intent shall declare a JSON Schema for its response and the AI pipeline shall reject any response that does not validate against that schema; raw XML responses from the model shall never be accepted.

hlr.name: Validate-then-Retry Loop
hlr.text: The AI pipeline shall apply each schema-valid response as a JSON Patch on a copy of the tree, run XSD plus lint, and on failure retry up to `projectXml.ai.maxRetries` times with the validator's findings fed back as a correction prompt; once the budget is exhausted the suggestion and the failures shall be surfaced to the user instead of being written.

hlr.name: Diff Preview Before Write
hlr.text: No AI-authored edit shall be persisted to `doc/Project.xml` without first being shown to the user in a diff preview that the user explicitly accepts; `projectXml.ai.autoApplyValidated` shall default to false and shall be honoured even for fully-validated suggestions.

hlr.name: AI Provenance Logging
hlr.text: Each accepted or rejected AI suggestion shall be appended to `.edit_doc/ai_history.jsonl` with timestamp, intent name, model identifier, prompt hash, accept/reject outcome, and final validator state, when `projectXml.ai.logHistory` is enabled.

hlr.name: Graceful Degradation Without an AI Model
hlr.text: When no language model is available (`vscode.lm.selectChatModels` returns an empty set), every AI surface shall hide itself cleanly — chat participant unregistered, AI-suggest Quick Fixes suppressed, AI commands hidden — and every deterministic surface (tree, diagnostics, code lenses, form panels, render, Stage A merge) shall continue to function unchanged.

hlr.name: AI Surfaces Disabled in Untrusted Workspaces
hlr.text: The extension shall declare `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` and shall block activation of every AI surface (chat participant, right-click actions, AI Quick Fixes, AI-mediated merge resolution) until the user explicitly trusts the workspace; the deterministic surfaces shall remain available in untrusted mode.

hlr.name: AI-Assisted Drafting Across Every Payload Kind
hlr.text: The AI authoring pipeline shall provide a named drafting intent for every payload kind that contributes to a generated document — SDD modules and components (`draft.module`), HLRs (`draft.hlr`), LLRs (`draft.llr`), and tests (`draft.test`) — so that a developer can produce a schema-valid first draft of *any* element in the SDD → HLR → LLR → Test stack from natural language plus the existing project context, without leaving the editor and without ever hand-authoring XML.

hlr.name: AI-Assisted Expansion Down the Stack
hlr.text: The AI pipeline shall provide expansion intents that walk the SDD → HLR → LLR → Test stack: `expand.hlr_to_llrs` shall draft a candidate set of LLRs for a selected HLR with traces pre-populated, and an equivalent intent shall draft test purposes for a selected LLR with traces pre-populated. Each expansion result shall pass through the same XSD + lint pipeline as a manual edit before any write.

hlr.name: AI-Assisted Review of Every Item
hlr.text: The AI pipeline shall provide a `review.item` intent that, given any HLR, LLR, test, or SDD module, returns advisory findings about clarity, completeness, and alignment with the upstream item it traces to (PVD vision for HLRs, HLR for LLRs, LLR/HLR for tests, SDD design goals for modules). Review output shall be advisory only — surfaced in the chat participant or as inline diagnostics — and shall never apply edits without an explicit user accept.

hlr.name: AI-Assisted Trace Suggestion and Gap Fill
hlr.text: The AI pipeline shall provide a `suggest.traces` intent that, given a payload element, proposes plausible upstream `<trace>` targets and a `gap.fix` intent that, given a coverage-gap warning from the linter, drafts the missing LLR or test that would close it. Both intents shall pre-fill the suggestion with stable IDs and route through the validate-then-retry pipeline before any write.

hlr.name: AI-Assisted PVD Ghostwriting
hlr.text: The AI pipeline shall provide a guided ghostwriting flow for the hand-authored `doc/PVD.md`: when a developer asks for help on the PVD, the AI shall identify thin or missing sections by structure (placeholders, single-sentence sections expected to be paragraphs, lists with one item where multiple are expected), ask the developer targeted questions to elicit direction, and only then draft prose in the existing voice and heading style. AI shall never invent product direction (vision, scope, success metrics, roadmap) without the developer's explicit answer, and PVD edits shall pass through the same diff-preview gate as Project.xml edits ([HLR-032](#HLR-032)).

hlr.name: AI Surfaces in the Project Spec Tree
hlr.text: Every node in the "Project Spec" tree view that represents a payload element shall offer the applicable AI authoring actions (`Draft / Expand / Review / Suggest traces / Fix gap with AI`) as context-menu commands derived from the schema's UI-hint registry; the available actions per node shall be discovered from the registry, not hard-coded per element kind, so a new payload kind gains the AI surface for free.

section.title: Structured Merge Resolution
section.intro: Requirements covering the two-stage merge pipeline ([SDD §9](SDD.md#9) deterministic Stage A, [SDD §20](SDD.md#20) AI-mediated Stage B). All Phase 5.5 deliverables in [SDP](SDP.md).

hlr.name: Deterministic Structural Merge (Stage A)
hlr.text: The structured merger shall perform a deterministic three-way merge keyed by the stable identifiers of every payload element, shall union additions whose IDs do not collide, shall union `<traces>` entries by `(target, ref)` tuple, and shall recompute `<metadata>/<counts>` from the merged tree.

hlr.name: Residual Conflict Reporting
hlr.text: Stage A shall emit overlapping body edits, divergent trace targets, ID renames, and schema-version bumps as a structured list of residual `Conflict` records rather than guessing a resolution; the AI pipeline (Stage B) consumes that list.

hlr.name: Merge Editor Integration
hlr.text: The extension shall expose `projectXml.resolveMergeConflicts`, shall pull the `:1`/`:2`/`:3` blobs of `doc/Project.xml` via the `git` extension API, shall call `merge_three_way`, and shall present each Stage B suggestion as a distinct region in VS Code's three-way merge editor that the user accepts or rejects per region; merge resolutions shall never auto-land.

section.title: Developer and CI Tooling
section.intro: Requirements covering the convenience tooling layer ([SDD §7 Makefile](SDD.md#7)) and the operational invariants that keep CI healthy.

hlr.name: Cross-Platform Prerequisite Installation
hlr.text: `tools/Makefile` shall detect the host OS family from `uname -s` plus `/etc/os-release` (`debian`, `fedora`, `arch`, `macos`) and dispatch to a matching `prereqs-*` recipe that installs the toolchain documented in [SDP §0](SDP.md), with sudo auto-detected so the same recipes work for a developer with `sudo` and for a CI container running as root.

hlr.name: Slim CI Prerequisites Path
hlr.text: `tools/Makefile` shall provide a `prereqs-ci` target that installs only the headless toolchain (Python, Node, libxml2, git) and omits VS Code, `vsce`, and `gh` so headless CI runners do not pull desktop binaries unnecessarily.

hlr.name: CI Umbrella Target
hlr.text: `tools/Makefile` shall provide a `ci` umbrella target that runs lint, XSD validation, render of every generated document, the pytest suite under `test/`, and the VS Code extension type-check + bundle, in fail-fast order; CI shall invoke this single target.

hlr.name: Reproducible Project Bootstrap
hlr.text: `tools/Makefile bootstrap` shall create a per-project Python venv at `.venv`, install the renderer/linter/test dependencies (jinja2, lxml, pytest, xmlschema), run `npm install` in the VS Code extension directory, and install the `redhat.vscode-xml` extension when the `code` CLI is available; the target shall be idempotent so repeated invocations are safe.

section.title: Cross-Cutting Quality Attributes
section.intro: Cross-cutting requirements that span multiple components and encode the product principles in [PVD §6](PVD.md) that did not have a natural home in any single component-scoped section above.

hlr.name: Minimal Core Dependencies
hlr.text: The renderer (`tools/render_doc.py`) and the linter (`tools/lint_project.py`) shall depend only on the Python standard library plus Jinja2 on the spec-generation hot path; rich-XML facilities (`lxml`, `xmllint`) shall remain optional and the linter shall degrade gracefully when they are absent so a fresh checkout can render and validate every generated document without any extra installs beyond `pip install jinja2`.

hlr.name: Self-Verification of TraceR's Own Spec Stack
hlr.text: TraceR shall ship with its own populated `doc/Project.xml`, fully generated SDD/HLRs/LLRs/STP/Traceability documents, and a self-applied lint pass; the repository's own `ci` target (see [HLR-039](#HLR-039)) shall fail when its own `doc/Project.xml` lints with any error or when any generated document is out of date with respect to the source XML.

function.title: `parse_project_to_dict` ([tools/render_doc.py](../tools/render_doc.py))
function.name: parse_project_to_dict
function.intro: The library entry point that loads `Project.xml` and returns the parsed payload as a JSON-serialisable dict. The JSON-RPC sidecar's `parse_to_json` method, the form-panel JSON Schema deriver, and the structured merger all consume this surface; templates consume the equivalent `SimpleNamespace` form via `load_project`.

llr.text: `parse_project_to_dict` shall accept an `xml_path` argument that defaults to the canonical `doc/Project.xml` location so that callers operating on the repository's own spec stack do not need to know the path.

`parse_project_to_dict` shall raise `ProjectXmlError` (never `SystemExit`) on a missing file or malformed XML so that library callers (`project_io.py`, the test suite, the Phase 5.5 merger) can handle the error without involving the CLI's process model.
