When the caller does not supply `metadata_for`, `parse_project_to_dict` shall pick the first `<metadata><document id="…">` entry as the metadata target so that callers wanting only structural data do not need to know which document id to ask for.

`parse_project_to_dict` shall expose every parsed payload — `sdd`, `stp`, `hlrs`, `llrs`, `tests`, plus the precomputed flat lists (`flat_hlrs`, `flat_llrs`, `flat_tests`) and id-based lookups (`hlr_by_id`, `llr_by_id`, `file_of_test`) and cross-reference indexes (`llrs_by_hlr`, `tests_by_hlr`, `tests_by_llr`, `hlrs_by_sdd`) — verbatim through the `_ns_to_jsonable` projection so the JSON-RPC surface, the schema-driven extension surfaces, and the test suite see exactly what templates see.

`parse_project_to_dict` shall depend only on `xml.etree.ElementTree` from the Python standard library for parsing — no `lxml`, no third-party XML dependency — so a fresh checkout can parse `Project.xml` without any extra installs beyond `pip install jinja2`.

function.title: `render_document` ([tools/render_doc.py](../tools/render_doc.py))
function.name: render_document
function.intro: The library entry point that renders one Markdown spec document from `Project.xml` plus a Jinja2 template. The CLI is a thin wrapper around it; the JSON-RPC sidecar's `render` method calls it directly.

llr.text: `render_document` shall raise `ProjectXmlError` when the requested template path does not exist, and never silently fall through to an empty render.

`render_document` shall select the metadata block by the `metadata_id` argument so each `<metadata><document id="…">` entry maps to exactly one rendered document; an unknown id shall raise `ProjectXmlError`.

`render_document` shall return Markdown normalised to exactly one trailing newline regardless of the template's whitespace so the CLI, the sidecar's `render` method, the in-memory preview pane, and the on-disk `--out` write produce byte-identical output for the same `(template, metadata_id, xml_path)` triple.

`render_document` shall expose the `gh_slug` filter and the `project.*` cross-reference indexes documented in [doc/Schema_Reference.md §9](Schema_Reference.md) on every render so templates can link to SDD section anchors and traverse the SDD → HLR → LLR → Test stack without recomputing relations in Jinja.
`render_document` shall depend only on the Python standard library plus Jinja2; no XSD validator, no `lxml`, no language-model client may be imported from the render hot path.

function.title: `init_project` ([tools/render_doc.py](../tools/render_doc.py))
function.name: init_project
function.intro: The bootstrap entry point that turns a fresh checkout into a populated `doc/Project.xml` plus `doc/PVD.md` skeleton.

llr.text: `init_project` shall write a schema-1.1 skeleton `Project.xml` containing populated `<metadata>` (with one `<document>` row per baseline generated document) plus empty `<sdd>`, `<stp>`, `<hlrs>`, `<llrs>`, and `<tests>` payloads so the resulting file lints cleanly and can be opened in the VS Code extension immediately.

`init_project` shall substitute `tools/templates/PVD.md.template` into a new `doc/PVD.md` with the project name, short name, author, and date placeholders replaced; the resulting PVD shall contain the section skeleton enumerated in [.github/skills/project-xml/SKILL.md](../.github/skills/project-xml/SKILL.md) so the AI ghostwriting flow has a structural target.

`init_project` shall refuse to overwrite either target file when `force` is false and shall raise `ProjectXmlError` listing which file already exists, so a misconfigured invocation cannot silently destroy hand-authored content.

`init_project` shall compute a relative `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` from the new `Project.xml`'s parent directory to `tools/project.xsd` when the caller does not supply `schema_location` so XSD-aware editors (Red Hat XML, the Phase 1 extension's host) resolve the schema with no further configuration.

function.title: `lint` ([tools/lint_project.py](../tools/lint_project.py))
function.name: lint
function.intro: The library entry point of the linter; both the CLI and the JSON-RPC sidecar's `lint` method delegate to it.

llr.text: `lint` shall return a `Findings` object aggregating `errors`, `warnings`, and `notes` lists so callers can present each severity independently and compute `ok = (errors == [])` without re-walking the message list.

`lint` shall run structural validation first and shall short-circuit semantic checks if the document fails to parse, so a malformed `Project.xml` does not produce a cascade of misleading "unknown id" errors that mask the real problem.

`lint` shall surface every coverage gap (HLRs with no LLR or test, LLRs with no test) as a warning rather than an error so that an honest gap can ride in `Traceability.md` without blocking CI, while still being visible in the Problems panel and in the rendered Traceability Matrix.

`lint` shall be a pure function over `(xml_path, xsd_path)` — no `print`, no `sys.exit`, no environmental I/O beyond reading the two paths — so the JSON-RPC sidecar, the test suite, and the future status-bar item can call it from a single process without spawning a subprocess.

function.title: `validate_structure` ([tools/lint_project.py](../tools/lint_project.py))
function.name: validate_structure
function.intro: The XSD-validation wrapper that drives the lxml → xmllint → structural-only fallback chain.

llr.text: `validate_structure` shall attempt validation using `lxml.etree.XMLSchema` first when the `lxml` import succeeds, so that strict, in-process XSD validation is the default path on machines that have it installed.

When `lxml` is unavailable, `validate_structure` shall fall back to invoking `xmllint --noout --schema <xsd> <xml>` via `subprocess.run` and shall translate its non-zero exit into one error finding per reported diagnostic line.

When neither `lxml` nor `xmllint` is available, `validate_structure` shall degrade to a well-formedness-only pass and shall record an explicit note ("not XSD-validated; install lxml or xmllint for full validation") so the user is never silently told the document is valid when no validator ran.

`validate_structure` shall always emit a note naming which validator path actually ran (`lxml`, `xmllint`, or `structural-only`) so that a CI failure or a Problems-panel surprise can be traced back to the validator in use.

function.title: `check_semantics` ([tools/lint_project.py](../tools/lint_project.py))
function.name: check_semantics
function.intro: Semantic checks layered on top of structural validation: id format and uniqueness, trace reference resolution, metadata completeness, and coverage gaps.

llr.text: `check_semantics` shall reject any HLR id that does not match the `^HLR-\d{3,}$` pattern and any LLR id that does not match the `^LLR-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{2,}$` pattern as a hard error so that ID format breaks CI rather than degrading silently into a coverage gap.

`check_semantics` shall report every duplicate `HLR-NNN` or `LLR-XXX-NN` id as an error naming both the duplicate id and (where available) the line of the offending element so the user can navigate directly to it.

`check_semantics` shall resolve every `<trace target="HLR" ref="…"/>` against the set of HLR ids and every `<trace target="LLR" ref="…"/>` against the set of LLR ids; an unresolved reference shall produce an error finding that quotes the missing id and the citing element so the user can fix it without searching the file.

`check_semantics` shall classify `<trace target="SDD" ref="…"/>` references as warnings (rather than errors) when the `ref` does not look like a dotted SDD section id (`^\d+(\.\d+)*$`), reflecting that SDD sections are weakly resolvable until the renderer's section catalogue is reached.

`check_semantics` shall compute coverage gaps from the parsed tree — HLRs with no LLR or test linking to them, LLRs with no test linking to them — and shall emit one warning per gap so that the rendered Traceability Matrix and the Problems panel see the same set.

`check_semantics` shall verify that every document id referenced by a Jinja2 template under `tools/templates/` has a matching `<metadata><document id="…">` entry; missing entries shall be reported as errors and duplicate document ids shall be reported as errors.

function.title: `serve` and `handle_request` ([tools/project_io.py](../tools/project_io.py))
function.name: serve
function.intro: The JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatch loop and the per-method handler dispatcher that together implement the long-running sidecar.

llr.text: `serve` shall read line-delimited JSON requests from stdin and write line-delimited JSON responses to stdout, flushing after each response, so a client that opens stdin/stdout pipes and writes one request per line gets exactly one response per line in the same order.
`serve` shall ignore blank input lines and shall exit cleanly with status 0 on EOF so the client can shut the sidecar down by closing stdin without needing a dedicated `shutdown` method.

`handle_request` shall return a JSON-RPC error with code `-32700` (parse error) for any input that is not valid JSON, with code `-32600` (invalid request) when `method` is missing or non-string, and with code `-32601` (method not found) when the method name is unknown — exactly matching the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

`handle_request` shall return code `-32602` (invalid params) for `ValueError` raised by a handler, code `-32000` (application error) for `ProjectXmlError`, and code `-32603` (internal error) for any other uncaught exception so that user-fixable errors are distinguishable from sidecar bugs by the client.

`handle_request` shall correlate every response with its request by echoing the request's `id` field verbatim (including `null`), and shall suppress the response entirely when the request is a JSON-RPC notification (`jsonrpc=="2.0"` and no `id` key).

`handle_request` shall dispatch every method through the `METHODS` registry rather than via per-method `if`/`elif` branches so adding a new method is a single registry-table edit and the JSON-RPC error machinery applies uniformly.

The `METHODS` registry shall map `lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, and `init_project` to thin wrappers around the corresponding `tools/render_doc.py` / `tools/lint_project.py` library functions; no method handler shall reimplement parsing, rendering, or linting logic in `project_io.py`.

function.title: `activate` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/extension.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/extension.ts))
function.name: activate
function.intro: The VS Code extension entry point that wires every Phase 1-2 surface (sidecar client, tree view, lint diagnostics, code lenses, render & preview, reveal-in-XML) into a single activation pass.

llr.text: `activate` shall construct the `ProjectIoClient`, register every contributed command, and create the `Project Spec` tree view, the lint `DiagnosticCollection`, the `tracer-preview:` content provider, and the coverage code-lens provider — pushing each onto `context.subscriptions` so they are torn down deterministically on extension deactivate.

`activate` shall register the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` first and pass it to every component that may report a sidecar or parse failure so the user can diagnose interpreter / workspace problems without leaving the editor.

`activate` shall subscribe to `vscode.workspace.onDidSaveTextDocument` and, when the saved document is the configured `Project.xml`, refresh the tree, refresh the code-lens cache, optionally re-run `lint` (gated on `projectXml.autoLintOnChange`), and optionally invalidate the preview cache (gated on `projectXml.previewOnSave`).

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: The extension manifest shall declare `redhat.vscode-xml` as an `extensionDependencies` entry and `untrustedWorkspaces.supported = "limited"` so XSD-backed XML editing comes for free and the deterministic Phase 1-2 surfaces remain available in untrusted workspaces while AI surfaces (Phase 5) can gate themselves off.

trace.name: AI Surfaces Disabled in Untrusted Workspaces

function.title: `ProjectIoClient` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts))
function.name: ProjectIoClient
function.intro: The long-running JSON-RPC 2.0 client wrapping `tools/project_io.py`. Every TypeScript surface (tree, diagnostics, lenses, render commands, preview content provider) routes through it.

llr.text: `ProjectIoClient` shall spawn `tools/project_io.py` lazily on first request — never during construction — so importing the module does not require a Python interpreter to be installed and `activate` stays cheap.

`ProjectIoClient.request` shall correlate every JSON-RPC response with its sender by allocating a monotonically-increasing numeric `id`, parking the resolver in a pending-map, and resolving / rejecting it when the line with the matching `id` arrives on stdout — so multiple in-flight requests do not deadlock.

`ProjectIoClient` shall reject every pending request with the same exit error when the sidecar process exits unexpectedly, and shall surface JSON-RPC error responses as `SidecarError(code, message)` so callers can switch on the JSON-RPC error code without parsing message text.

`ProjectIoClient` shall pipe every byte the sidecar writes to stderr into the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` prefixed with `[sidecar:stderr]`, so Python tracebacks are visible to the user without leaving the editor.

`ProjectIoClient.dispose` shall close the sidecar's stdin and kill the child process, and the same cleanup shall run automatically on extension deactivate via the `context.subscriptions` machinery so the sidecar never outlives the extension.

`ProjectIoClient` shall pick the Python interpreter from the `projectXml.pythonPath` setting first and fall back to `python3` (POSIX) or `python` (Windows) so users with a project venv can point the sidecar at it without editing the extension source.

function.title: `ProjectSpecProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/treeView/ProjectSpecProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/treeView/ProjectSpecProvider.ts))
function.name: ProjectSpecProvider
function.intro: The Phase 1 hand-written tree provider that contributes the `Project Spec` Activity Bar view rooted at `Project.xml`. Phase 2.5 will rewrite the per-payload builders to walk the schema-driven hint registry.

llr.text: `ProjectSpecProvider.getChildren` shall return one root `ProjectSpecNode` per top-level payload (HLRs, LLRs, Tests, SDD, STP) when invoked with no element, with each root labelled with a count derived from the parsed tree (e.g. `HLRs (45)`).

`ProjectSpecProvider` shall populate the tree by calling `ProjectIoClient.parseToJson` exactly once per refresh and caching the result; `refresh()` shall clear the cache and fire `onDidChangeTreeData` so VS Code re-requests the children.

Every leaf `ProjectSpecNode` mapping to a real `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, `<test>`, or `<module>` element shall carry a `RevealLocator` payload `{tag, attr?, value}` and shall set `contextValue = "revealable"` so the Reveal-in-XML command and the context menu can target it precisely.

When `parse_to_json` fails, `ProjectSpecProvider.getChildren` shall return a single error node (themed with `error` icon) bearing the error message rather than throwing, so the tree still renders and the user sees an actionable explanation in the Activity Bar.

function.title: `LintDiagnosticsProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/diagnostics/LintDiagnosticsProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/diagnostics/LintDiagnosticsProvider.ts))
function.name: LintDiagnosticsProvider
function.intro: Mirrors lint findings from `project_io.lint` into a VS Code `DiagnosticCollection` over `Project.xml`. Phase 2.5's stable-`code` retrofit and Quick Fix table layer on top of this Phase 1 surface.

llr.text: `LintDiagnosticsProvider.run` shall call `ProjectIoClient.lint` with the configured `xml_path` and (when set) `xsd_path`, and shall replace the entire `DiagnosticCollection` for `Project.xml` on success so the Problems panel reflects the latest lint state without requiring the user to clear stale entries.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: `LintDiagnosticsProvider.publish` shall map each `Findings.errors` entry to `DiagnosticSeverity.Error`, each warning to `DiagnosticSeverity.Warning`, and each note to `DiagnosticSeverity.Information` — preserving every finding verbatim so warnings are never silently downgraded or hidden.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: Each `Diagnostic` shall be anchored to a best-effort range computed by `rangeForFinding(doc, message)` (HLR/LLR id token first, quoted attribute value second, `<element>` mention third, file head as fallback) and shall set `source = "projectXml"` so users can filter the Problems panel to the linter's output.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

llr.text: When `ProjectIoClient.lint` rejects (interpreter missing, sidecar exited), `LintDiagnosticsProvider.run` shall publish a single top-of-file `Error` diagnostic carrying the failure message rather than swallowing the rejection silently, so the user sees the failure in the Problems panel and the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` simultaneously.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

function.title: `revealInXml` and `locator` helpers ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: revealInXml
function.intro: The Phase 1 jump-to-element command, plus the regex-based locator helpers it uses to range XML elements without parsing the file in TypeScript.

llr.text: `revealInXml` shall accept either a `ProjectSpecNode` (from a tree-view context-menu invocation) or a bare `RevealLocator` (from the code-lens click path) and shall dispatch through `findIdRange` / `findAttrRange` / `findElementRange` so every caller takes the same locator code path.

`findIdRange` shall match `<TAG ... id="ID">` via regex, return a `vscode.Range` over the `id="..."` attribute value (not the whole tag), and never fall through to a wrong element when two elements share an id substring (the regex anchors on `\bid="ID"`).

When the locator cannot find the requested element, `revealInXml` shall still open `Project.xml` in a non-preview editor and shall surface a warning toast describing what was not found (`<llr id="LLR-PCL-04"> not found in Project.xml`) so the user has both the file and an actionable explanation.

`rangeForFinding` shall scan a finding message for `HLR-NNN` ids first, then `LLR-XXX-NN` ids, then quoted attribute values, then `<element>` mentions, and shall return the first hit's range — falling back to the file head only when none match — so diagnostic underlines target the most specific token available.

trace.name: Lint Diagnostics in the Problems Panel

function.title: `renderAndPreview` and `MarkdownPreviewProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: renderAndPreview
function.intro: The Phase 2 side-by-side Markdown preview surface: a `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` content provider plus the command that opens it via `markdown.showPreviewToSide`.

llr.text: `renderAndPreview` shall accept an optional `docId` (string or `{docId}` object) argument, prompt the user with a QuickPick over `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` when none is supplied, and refuse with a warning toast when the supplied id is not in `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` — never falling through to a partial render.

`renderAndPreview` shall mark the preview cache stale for the chosen `docId` and then dispatch `vscode.commands.executeCommand("markdown.showPreviewToSide", uri)` so the user always sees content rendered against the current `Project.xml` state, not a cached snapshot.

`MarkdownPreviewProvider` shall register the `tracer-preview` URI scheme via `vscode.workspace.registerTextDocumentContentProvider` and shall serve content for `tracer-preview:/<doc-id>.md` URIs by calling `ProjectIoClient.render` — so no preview path ever writes a Markdown file under `doc/`.

`MarkdownPreviewProvider.markStale(docId?)` shall drop the cached markdown for `docId` (or every tracked preview when called with no argument) and shall fire `onDidChange` for each tracked id so VS Code re-requests content; the on-save handler in `activate` shall call this when `projectXml.previewOnSave` is enabled.

When `ProjectIoClient.render` rejects, `MarkdownPreviewProvider.provideTextDocumentContent` shall return a `# Project Spec preview — render failed` Markdown body quoting the error (and append the failure to the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel`) rather than throwing, so the preview pane always shows actionable text instead of crashing the host.

function.title: `renderAll` and `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/))
function.name: renderAll
function.intro: The Phase 2 batch-regeneration command, plus the single named constant Phase 2.5 will swap for a `list_documents` sidecar call.

llr.text: `renderAll` shall iterate `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` and shall call `ProjectIoClient.render` for each entry with the `out` parameter set to the corresponding workspace-relative `source` path so each generated Markdown is written by the sidecar (never assembled in TypeScript).

`renderAll` shall display a progress notification while it runs, shall continue past per-document failures (collecting them into a failure list rather than aborting on the first error), and shall summarise both the success count and the failed document ids in the closing toast.

`renderAll` shall call `MarkdownPreviewProvider.markStale()` (with no argument) at the end of every run so any preview pane the user opened earlier in the session refreshes against the new on-disk state.

`BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` shall be the single named source of truth for the Phase 2 hard-coded document set (`SDD`, `HLRs`, `LLRs`, `STP`, `Traceability`); every consumer (the `renderAll` loop, the `renderAndPreview` QuickPick, the `MarkdownPreviewProvider` doc-id lookup) shall import this constant rather than enumerating ids inline so the Phase 2.5 swap to a `list_documents` sidecar call is a single-file edit.

function.title: `CoverageCodeLensProvider` ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeLens/CoverageCodeLensProvider.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/codeLens/CoverageCodeLensProvider.ts))
function.name: CoverageCodeLensProvider
function.intro: The Phase 2 code-lens provider that decorates `<hlr>`, `<llr>`, and `<test>` elements with coverage status and click-through reveal lenses. Phase 2.5 will replace the hard-coded element selectors with a walk over `ui_hints_index.lenses`.

llr.text: `CoverageCodeLensProvider.provideCodeLenses` shall return code lenses only when the active document's path equals the configured `Project.xml` so other XML files in the workspace are not decorated.

For every `<hlr id="…">` element the provider shall emit a summary lens whose title is `"<n> LLRs · <m> tests"` computed from the parsed tree's `<traces>` blocks (LLRs that trace to this HLR, plus tests that trace to it directly), and the analogous summary for every `<llr>` (`"<n> HLRs · <m> tests"`) and every `<test>` (`"<n> LLRs · <m> HLRs"`).

Each summary lens shall invoke a picker command (`projectXml.codeLens.pickRelated`) that opens a QuickPick over every related element; up to `MAX_INLINE_LENSES` related items shall additionally be emitted as inline `→ <id>` lenses that invoke `projectXml.revealInXml` with the per-related locator so the most common jumps are one click away.

An element with zero related items shall render the summary lens with title `"<n> LLRs · <m> tests — no coverage"` and an empty command so the user sees the gap without being given a useless click target; the provider shall not emit per-related inline lenses in this case.

`CoverageCodeLensProvider` shall cache the parsed project across consecutive `provideCodeLenses` invocations and shall coalesce concurrent in-flight `parseToJson` calls into a single sidecar request, so VS Code's per-keystroke lens-recompute does not fan out into N parallel sidecar calls.

`CoverageCodeLensProvider.refresh` shall drop the parsed-project cache and fire `onDidChangeCodeLenses` so a save (handled in `activate`) refreshes every lens range and label against the new on-disk state.

function.title: `paths` helpers ([tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts](../tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts))
function.name: paths
function.intro: Workspace-path resolution shared by every extension surface. Centralised here so the multi-root case and the `projectXml.*` settings overrides are handled in one place.

llr.text: `getProjectFolder` shall pick the open workspace folder whose root contains the configured `xmlPath` (default `doc/Project.xml`) so the extension works equally for a user who opens the TraceR repo root and for a user who opens a parent multi-root workspace.

`getProjectXmlPath`, `getXsdPath`, `getToolsDir`, and `getProjectIoScript` shall each resolve their result against `getProjectFolder()` when given a relative setting, return the value verbatim when given an absolute path, and return `undefined` only when no workspace folder is open — so callers can fail loudly with a single null check.

`describeWorkspaceState` shall return a single human-readable sentence explaining why path resolution failed (no workspace folder open, or `Project.xml` not found in any folder) so the sidecar's startup error message is actionable.

file.header: Tests for the importable surface of tools/render_doc.py: init_project (project bootstrap), load_project / parse_project_to_dict (the renderer's data surface), and render_document (the rendering primitive that the CLI, the JSON-RPC sidecar, and the extension's preview pane all consume).

test.name: test_creates_xml_and_pvd
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-01 and LLR-INI-02: `init_project` writes a schema-1.1 `Project.xml` skeleton with `name`, `short_name`, and `author` substituted, plus a `PVD.md` derived from the template with the placeholder text replaced.

test.name: test_refuses_overwrite_without_force
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-03: a second `init_project` call against an existing `Project.xml` raises `ProjectXmlError` rather than silently destroying the existing file.

test.name: test_force_overwrites_existing
test.purpose: Verifies the explicit `force=True` escape hatch in LLR-INI-03: the caller can opt back in to overwriting, and the `existing` list in the result names exactly the files that were replaced.

test.name: test_does_not_write_to_stderr
test.purpose: Verifies that `init_project` is a true library function (LLR-INI-01, LLR-PPD-02): it writes neither stdout nor stderr, leaving output policy to the caller.

test.name: test_load_known_metadata_id
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-01 and LLR-RND-02: `load_project` accepts a custom `xml_path` and selects the requested metadata id, returning the populated project namespace templates consume.

test.name: test_load_unknown_metadata_id_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-02: an unknown metadata id raises `ProjectXmlError` rather than falling through to a partial render or `KeyError`.

test.name: test_missing_file_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-02: a missing input file raises the library's `ProjectXmlError`, not `SystemExit` or a bare `FileNotFoundError`, so JSON-RPC handlers can map it to a JSON-RPC application error.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-02: `xml.etree.ElementTree.ParseError` from a truncated `<project><unclosed>` document is wrapped as `ProjectXmlError` with the original cause preserved.

test.name: test_returns_jsonable_dict
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-04: the `parse_project_to_dict` projection round-trips through `json.dumps` — no `SimpleNamespace` instances may leak into the JSON-RPC surface.

test.name: test_default_metadata_for_first_document
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PPD-03: with no `metadata_for` argument, the parser picks the first `<metadata><document>` entry (the skeleton's `SDD` row).

test.name: test_explicit_metadata_for_overrides
test.purpose: Verifies the `metadata_for` argument path of LLR-PPD-01 / LLR-PPD-03: an explicit id (`HLRs`) overrides the first-document default.

test.name: test_render_hlrs_returns_markdown_with_single_trailing_newline
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-03: `render_document` returns Markdown with exactly one trailing newline (never zero, never two), so the CLI, sidecar, and preview pane all emit byte-identical output.

test.name: test_missing_template_raises_project_xml_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-01: a missing template path raises `ProjectXmlError` rather than silently rendering an empty document.

test.name: test_writes_relative_schema_location_when_unset
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-04: when the caller does not supply `schema_location`, `init_project` writes a relative (never absolute) `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` resolving to `project.xsd`, so XSD-aware editors find the schema with no further configuration.

test.name: test_explicit_schema_location_overrides_default
test.purpose: Verifies the explicit override path of LLR-INI-04: an explicit `schema_location` argument is written verbatim into the skeleton's `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`.

test.name: test_rendered_document_uses_gh_slug_anchor
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RND-04: rendering an HLRs document end-to-end exercises the `gh_slug` filter and the `project.*` cross-reference indexes; if either were missing the render would have raised before producing output.

test.name: test_gh_slug_filter_is_registered_on_jinja_env
test.purpose: Pins LLR-RND-04 directly: a one-shot probe template that pipes a string through `gh_slug` round-trips to the expected slug, and the underlying `_gh_slug` helper produces the same value when called directly.

file.header: Tests for the importable surface of tools/lint_project.py: the `lint` entry point, the `Findings` dataclass, and the human-readable `Findings.report` formatter consumed by both the CLI and the JSON-RPC sidecar.

test.name: test_lint_returns_findings_object
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-01: `lint` returns a `Findings` instance (not a tuple, not a dict) so callers consume `.errors`, `.warnings`, `.notes`, and `.ok` by attribute.

test.name: test_findings_to_dict_is_jsonable
test.purpose: Verifies that `Findings.to_dict()` is JSON-serialisable (it is the JSON-RPC `lint` method's return shape) and contains exactly the documented `errors`/`warnings`/`notes` keys, each holding a list.

test.name: test_skeleton_has_no_errors
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-01 and LLR-LNT-02: a freshly-bootstrapped `Project.xml` lints with zero errors (warnings for empty payloads are acceptable).

test.name: test_missing_file_records_error_no_stderr
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-04: `lint` is a pure function — a missing file is recorded as a `Findings.errors` entry, never written to stderr; redirected stderr remains empty.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_records_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-02: structural validation runs first; a malformed XML document records an error finding and short-circuits the semantic checks instead of producing a cascade of misleading "unknown id" diagnostics.

test.name: test_real_repo_project_xml_lints
test.purpose: Smoke test against the live `doc/Project.xml`: the project's own source-of-truth must lint with zero error findings (warnings for unbuilt-phase coverage gaps are acceptable per HLR-014/HLR-042).

test.name: test_report_writes_to_supplied_stream
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-LNT-04 and HLR-042: `Findings.report` writes errors, warnings, and notes verbatim to the caller-supplied stream and ends with a `N error(s)` summary line — warnings are surfaced, never silently dropped.

test.name: test_report_suppresses_warnings_when_disabled
test.purpose: Verifies the explicit `show_warnings=False` API: callers (CI scripts, CLI flag) can opt out of warning text in the report stream, but the warnings remain in the underlying `Findings` collection so the JSON-RPC surface still sees them.

test.name: test_malformed_xml_records_error_and_returns_none
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-01: structural validation runs first; a malformed XML payload short-circuits the validator chain, records a `malformed XML` error, and returns `None` so semantic checks do not run on a broken tree.

test.name: test_lxml_path_is_preferred_when_available
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-01: when `_try_lxml_validate` succeeds, `validate_structure` does not consult `xmllint` and emits no degraded-mode note.

test.name: test_xmllint_fallback_when_lxml_unavailable
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-02: when `lxml` is unavailable, `validate_structure` falls back to `_try_xmllint_validate` and proceeds without emitting the structural-only note.

test.name: test_structural_only_emits_explicit_note
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-VST-03: when neither `lxml` nor `xmllint` is available, `validate_structure` returns the well-formedness-only tree and records exactly one explicit note saying that XSD validation was skipped.

test.name: test_bad_hlr_id_format_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-01: an HLR id that does not match `HLR-NNN` is reported as a hard error naming the offending id and the expected pattern.

test.name: test_bad_llr_id_format_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-01: an LLR id that does not match `LLR-XXX-NN` is reported as a hard error naming the offending id and the expected pattern.

test.name: test_duplicate_hlr_id_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-02: every duplicate `HLR-NNN` id is reported as an error naming the duplicated id.

test.name: test_duplicate_llr_id_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-02: every duplicate `LLR-XXX-NN` id is reported as an error naming the duplicated id.

test.name: test_unknown_hlr_trace_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-03: an LLR whose `<trace target="HLR" ref="..."/>` cites a non-existent HLR id produces an error quoting the missing id.

test.name: test_unknown_llr_trace_from_test_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-03: a test whose `<trace target="LLR" ref="..."/>` cites a non-existent LLR id produces an error quoting the missing id.

test.name: test_non_dotted_sdd_ref_is_a_warning_not_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-04: an SDD trace `ref` that does not match a dotted section pattern produces a warning rather than an error, reflecting that SDD section ids are weakly resolvable.

test.name: test_coverage_gap_for_uncovered_llr_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05 and LLR-LNT-03: an LLR with no test traces produces exactly one `has no test verifying it` warning and no error finding.

test.name: test_coverage_gap_for_uncovered_hlr_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05 and LLR-LNT-03: an HLR with no direct test and no LLR-mediated coverage produces a `has no test verifying it` warning rather than an error.

test.name: test_hlr_covered_indirectly_via_llr_test_is_not_a_gap
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-05: an HLR is considered covered when at least one of its LLRs has a test, so no gap warning is emitted in the indirect-coverage case.

test.name: test_missing_metadata_document_is_a_warning
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-06: a `<metadata>` block missing one of the standard `<document id="..."/>` rows produces a warning per missing id naming the absent document.

test.name: test_duplicate_metadata_document_is_an_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SEM-06: duplicate `<document id="..."/>` entries within `<metadata>` are reported as errors naming the duplicated id.

file.header: Tests for the JSON-RPC surface in tools/project_io.py. Exercises both the in-process handle_request() entry point and the end-to-end stdin/stdout subprocess form (the SubprocessTests class spawns the real `python3 tools/project_io.py` so it covers the same wire path the VS Code extension uses).

test.name: test_lint_method_returns_findings
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and HLR-016: the `lint` method dispatches through the registry, returns a JSON-RPC response with `result` containing `errors`/`warnings`/`notes`/`ok`, and echoes the request's `id`.

test.name: test_lint_matches_cli_findings
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and HLR-043 (cross-surface output equivalence): the in-process `lint_project.lint` library and the JSON-RPC `lint` method return byte-identical errors/warnings/notes for the same `Project.xml`.

test.name: test_render_method_returns_markdown
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-RND-03: the `render` method delegates to `render_document` and returns a `result` whose `output` ends with exactly one newline and whose `out_path` is `null` when no `out` parameter is supplied.

test.name: test_render_writes_to_out_path
test.purpose: Verifies the `out` parameter path of LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-RAL-01: when `out` is supplied, the sidecar writes the rendered Markdown to that path and echoes the path in `result.out_path`.

test.name: test_parse_to_json_returns_dict
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-PPD-04: the `parse_to_json` method delegates to `parse_project_to_dict` and the response round-trips through `json.dumps`.

test.name: test_init_project_method
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-07 and LLR-INI-01: the `init_project` method delegates to `render_doc.init_project`, writes the new files, and echoes the destination paths in the response.

test.name: test_init_project_refuses_overwrite
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-INI-03 and LLR-SRV-04: `init_project`'s overwrite guard surfaces as a JSON-RPC `APPLICATION_ERROR` (-32000) rather than as a server crash.

test.name: test_unknown_method_returns_method_not_found
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: an unknown method name produces JSON-RPC `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` (-32601) per the spec.

test.name: test_missing_method_returns_invalid_request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: a request object with no `method` key produces JSON-RPC `INVALID_REQUEST` (-32600) per the spec.

test.name: test_invalid_params_returns_invalid_params
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-04: a `render` call missing required parameters surfaces as JSON-RPC `INVALID_PARAMS` (-32602), distinguishing user error from sidecar bug.

test.name: test_application_error_for_bad_xml_path
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-04: a `render` call against a non-existent `xml_path` surfaces as JSON-RPC `APPLICATION_ERROR` (-32000) so the client can distinguish a fixable user error from an `INTERNAL_ERROR` (-32603) sidecar bug.

test.name: test_notification_returns_none
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-05: a JSON-RPC notification (`jsonrpc=="2.0"`, no `id`) returns `None` from `handle_request` so the serve loop emits no response line for it.

test.name: test_multiple_requests_one_per_line
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-01 and LLR-SRV-05: `serve` processes line-delimited requests in order and writes one response per line, with the response `id` matching the request `id` for each.

test.name: test_invalid_json_returns_parse_error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-03: a non-JSON line produces JSON-RPC `PARSE_ERROR` (-32700) per the spec.

test.name: test_blank_lines_ignored_and_eof_returns_zero
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-02: `serve` ignores blank input lines (no response is written for any of them) and returns exit code 0 on EOF — the documented clean-shutdown path the VS Code extension relies on.

test.name: test_methods_registry_contains_documented_methods
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06 and LLR-SRV-07: the `METHODS` registry table holds exactly the documented method names (`lint`, `render`, `parse_to_json`, `init_project`) and every value is callable.

test.name: test_dispatch_routes_through_methods_table
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06: registering a stub handler at runtime makes a brand-new method dispatchable through `handle_request` without any change to the dispatcher — proving the dispatcher consults `METHODS` rather than a hard-coded if/elif chain.

test.name: test_unknown_method_after_unregister_returns_method_not_found
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-SRV-06: removing a method from the registry makes it unreachable (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) without any code change in `handle_request` — the symmetric proof that dispatch is registry-driven.

test.name: test_echo_lint_request_returns_findings
test.purpose: End-to-end integration test that spawns the real `python3 tools/project_io.py` subprocess, sends one JSON-RPC `lint` request on stdin, and verifies the response on stdout (LLR-SRV-01, HLR-016, HLR-021). This is the acceptance path the VS Code extension's `ProjectIoClient` exercises in production.

test.name: test_subprocess_lint_matches_in_process_lint
test.purpose: Cross-surface equivalence pin (HLR-043): the spawned `python3 tools/project_io.py` subprocess returns byte-identical errors and warnings to the in-process `lint_project.lint` library for the same `Project.xml`.

file.header: Tier-1 (Mocha + ts-node, no VS Code host) unit tests for the BASELINE_DOCUMENTS catalogue and its helpers in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/documents.ts.

test.name: lists exactly the five Phase-2 baseline ids in the documented order
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01: `BASELINE_DOCUMENTS` is the single named source of truth for the Phase 2 hard-coded document set, in the documented `SDD`, `HLRs`, `LLRs`, `STP`, `Traceability` order.

test.name: every entry names a *.j2 template under tools/templates/
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01 / LLR-RAL-01: every catalogue entry points at a Jinja2 template under `tools/templates/`, so the `renderAll` loop has a valid template path for every id without further validation.

test.name: every entry writes to a doc/*.md path matching its id
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-BLD-01 / LLR-RAL-01: every catalogue entry writes to a `doc/*.md` path, matching the renderer's contract that the spec stack lives under `doc/`.

test.name: returns the entry with a matching id
test.purpose: Verifies the lookup contract used by `renderAndPreview` and the preview content provider: `findBaselineDocument` returns the entry whose id matches.

test.name: returns undefined for an unknown id
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RAP-01: `findBaselineDocument` returns `undefined` for an unknown id so `renderAndPreview` can refuse with a warning toast rather than fall through to a partial render.

test.name: templatePath joins toolsDir with templates/<file>
test.purpose: Verifies the path-join contract behind LLR-RAL-01: `templatePath(toolsDir, doc)` resolves to `<toolsDir>/templates/<doc.template>` so the sidecar render call sees a usable absolute path.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the regex-based locator in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/locator.ts. Drives the locator with a hand-constructed XML sample under a FakeTextDocument so the assertions cover real ranges without standing up a VS Code host.

test.name: targets the id="..." attribute, not the whole element
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RVX-02: `findIdRange` returns a range over the `id="..."` attribute value (not the whole tag), so the diagnostic underline and the reveal cursor land on the meaningful token.

test.name: disambiguates between elements that share an id substring
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RVX-02: the `\bid="ID"` anchoring distinguishes ids whose values overlap as substrings, so HLR-001 cannot be misreported as the location of HLR-002 (and vice versa).

test.name: returns undefined when the id is not present
test.purpose: Verifies the `undefined`-result contract of `findIdRange` that the reveal command depends on (LLR-RVX-03) so a missing id is reported via a warning toast, not a wrong-range jump.

test.name: findAttrRange locates a test by name
test.purpose: Verifies the `<test name="...">` location path of LLR-RVX-01: `findAttrRange` ranges a test by its `name` attribute so the tree-view reveal lands on the right test row.

test.name: findElementRange locates the opening tag of a payload
test.purpose: Verifies the `<element>`-mention fallback path of LLR-RVX-04: `findElementRange` ranges an opening tag so a finding that only mentions `<llrs>` still gets a precise underline.

test.name: prefers HLR ids over other tokens in the message
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-RVX-04: the scan order is HLR id first, then LLR id, then quoted attribute value, then `<element>` mention; an HLR token wins over an `<element>` token in the same message.

test.name: falls back to LLR id when no HLR matches
test.purpose: Verifies the LLR-id leg of the LLR-RVX-04 scan order: when no `HLR-NNN` token matches, the locator falls through to `LLR-XXX-NN`.

test.name: falls back to a quoted attribute value when no id matches
test.purpose: Verifies the quoted-attribute leg of LLR-RVX-04: when no HLR or LLR id is in the message, the locator targets the quoted attribute value (`'test_widget'`) rather than the file head.

test.name: falls back to file head when no token matches anything
test.purpose: Verifies the safe-default of LLR-RVX-04: when nothing in the message matches an id, an attribute value, or a tag mention, the locator returns a zero-length range at line 0 column 0 rather than throwing.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for tools/vscode-project-xml/src/util/paths.ts. Drives the workspace-folder and configuration helpers under the FakeWorkspace mock so the multi-root path-resolution rules can be asserted without a VS Code host.

test.name: returns undefined when no workspace folder is open
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-02: `getProjectFolder` returns `undefined` when no workspace folder is open, so callers can fail loudly with a single null check.

test.name: picks the folder that contains the configured xmlPath
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-01: in a multi-root workspace, `getProjectFolder` picks the folder whose root contains the configured `xmlPath`, not just the first folder in the list.

test.name: falls back to the first folder when no folder contains Project.xml
test.purpose: Verifies the documented fallback behaviour of LLR-PTH-01: when no open folder contains `Project.xml`, the helper returns the first folder so the user can still see an actionable error from the sidecar instead of a hard `undefined`.

test.name: resolves relative settings against the project folder
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-02: `getProjectXmlPath`, `getXsdPath`, `getToolsDir`, and `getProjectIoScript` each resolve their relative setting against `getProjectFolder()`'s root.

test.name: returns absolute settings verbatim
test.purpose: Verifies the absolute-path branch of LLR-PTH-02: a setting given as an absolute path is returned verbatim, so users with checkouts outside the workspace folder can point each helper at the right file directly.

test.name: returns undefined for every helper when no workspace folder is open
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-02: every path helper returns `undefined` (rather than throwing) when no workspace folder is open, so the sidecar startup error message can be shown via the standard `describeWorkspaceState` path.

test.name: explains the no-folder case in actionable terms
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-03: `describeWorkspaceState` returns a single human-readable sentence telling the user to open the TraceR folder, so the sidecar startup error is actionable from the Output channel alone.

test.name: names the missing Project.xml when folders are open
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PTH-03: when folders are open but `Project.xml` is not present in any of them, `describeWorkspaceState` names the missing file and the searched folders so the user knows which path to fix.

file.header: Tier-1 unit tests for the line-framing and dispatch path of ProjectIoClient in tools/vscode-project-xml/src/sidecar.ts. The framing is driven directly by feeding bytes to the private onStdout hook and probing the private pending map; this keeps the tests host-free and independent of the spawned Python sidecar.

test.name: dispatches a complete response line to the matching pending request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: pending resolvers are keyed by the response `id`, so a complete response line resolves exactly the matching pending promise and clears it from the in-flight map.

test.name: reassembles a response split across multiple chunks
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: the line buffer reassembles a JSON response that arrives split across multiple stdout chunks before dispatching it to the resolver.

test.name: dispatches multiple responses arriving in one chunk in id order
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: multiple responses delivered in a single stdout chunk are split on the newline boundary and dispatched to the correct resolvers, even when responses are returned out of request order.

test.name: rejects with SidecarError when the response carries an error object
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-03: a JSON-RPC error response surfaces as `SidecarError(code, message)` so callers can switch on the JSON-RPC error code without parsing message text.

test.name: ignores blank lines and unknown ids without disturbing pending requests
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-02: stray notifications and blank lines on the sidecar's stdout do not accidentally resolve a pending request.

test.name: logs invalid JSON lines and continues without rejecting any pending request
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-04: invalid JSON arriving on the sidecar's stdout is logged to the `Project Spec` `OutputChannel` and the dispatcher continues processing without rejecting any in-flight request.

test.name: failAll rejects every pending request with the supplied error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-03: when the sidecar process exits unexpectedly, every pending request is rejected with the same exit error rather than hanging the caller.

test.name: dispose rejects pending requests with a "sidecar disposed" error
test.purpose: Verifies LLR-PIC-05: `ProjectIoClient.dispose` rejects every pending request with a `sidecar disposed` error so callers do not leak promises across extension deactivate.

test.name: carries the JSON-RPC error code on a named SidecarError instance
test.purpose: Verifies the `SidecarError` constructor contract that LLR-PIC-03 depends on: the error carries the JSON-RPC `code`, identifies as `SidecarError` via its `name`, preserves the `message`, and is an `Error` subclass.
